+"""Packaging tests for the public Skills-only plugin builder and source freezer.
+
+These tests pin the fail-closed contract of ``tools/build_public_plugin.py`` and
+``tools/freeze_public_plugin_source.py``. Every case drives the REAL ``build_plugin(...)`` /
+``freeze(...)`` functions (never a re-implementation) and every case runs inside a private
+temporary directory: no network, no writes into the repository, nothing under ``dist/`` or
+``.hgk/``.
+
+They are also the historical red cases: they were written against the defect where the builder
+accepted a ``SKILL.md`` whose frontmatter ``name`` did not match its skill directory (the tool is
+fixed here, in ``project_skill_md``), and they pin the digest-pinnable, locally authored
+``plugin.schema.json`` subset that the builder validates the manifest with.
+
+Symlinks are exercised through the documented ``build_public_plugin._path_is_symlink`` seam when
+the host refuses to create a real symlink (unprivileged Windows), so the gate itself is always
+executed; where the OS allows the real thing, the real thing is used.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import functools
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+TOOLS = ROOT / "tools"
+if str(TOOLS) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS))
+
+import build_public_plugin as B  # noqa: E402  (sibling tool, stdlib-only)
+import freeze_public_plugin_source as F  # noqa: E402  (sibling tool, stdlib-only)
+
+SCHEMA_PATH = ROOT / "packaging" / "public-plugin" / "plugin.schema.json"
+CHECKED_IN_MANIFEST = ROOT / "packaging" / "public-plugin" / "plugin.json"
+GIT = shutil.which("git")
+
+COMMIT = "c" * 40
+TREE = "d" * 40
+PLUGIN_ID = "pipd-ls-sp-public-skills"
+SKILLS = tuple(F.EXPECTED_SKILLS)
+
+# The fixture frontmatter carries both portable and non-portable keys, exactly like the real packs.
+APPROVED_KEYS = ("name", "description", "license")
+DROPPED_KEYS = ("version", "owner", "triggers", "schemas", "references", "tests")
+
+FIXED_DATE_TIME = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
+FIXED_MODE = 0o644
+
+
+def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def skill_md_text(name: str, *, declared_name: str | None = None) -> str:
+    declared = name if declared_name is None else declared_name
+    return (
+        "---\n"
+        f"name: {declared}\n"
+        "description: Fixture skill for the public plugin packaging tests.\n"
+        "license: Apache-2.0\n"
+        "version: 1\n"
+        "owner: PIPD-EC (deterministic compiler)\n"
+        "triggers:\n"
+        "  - fixture trigger\n"
+        "schemas:\n"
+        "  - schemas/input.schema.json\n"
+        "references:\n"
+        "  - references/contract.md\n"
+        "tests:\n"
+        "  - tests/cases.yaml\n"
+        "---\n"
+        "\n"
+        f"# {name}\n"
+        "\n"
+        "## Contract (imperative)\n"
+        "\n"
+        "1. Keep the body byte-identical across the frontmatter projection.\n"
+        "2. Never let a packaging run touch a real repository tree.\n"
+    )
+
+
+class Env:
+    """A throwaway source checkout + packaging root, entirely under one temp directory."""
+
+    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
+        self.root = root
+        self.source = root / "source"
+        self.skills = self.source / "skills"
+        self.packaging = root / "packaging"
+        self.assets = self.packaging / "assets"
+        self.out = root / "release"
+        for name in SKILLS:
+            skill_dir = self.skills / name
+            skill_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            (skill_dir / "SKILL.md").write_text(skill_md_text(name), encoding="utf-8", newline="")
+        self.assets.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        # The real, checked-in local schema subset is what the builder must consume.
+        shutil.copyfile(SCHEMA_PATH, self.packaging / "plugin.schema.json")
+        (self.assets / "icon-128.png").write_bytes(B.png_icon_bytes(128))
+
+    @property
+    def schema_bytes(self) -> bytes:
+        return (self.packaging / "plugin.schema.json").read_bytes()
+
+    @property
+    def icon_bytes(self) -> bytes:
+        return (self.assets / "icon-128.png").read_bytes()
+
+    def freeze(self) -> dict:
+        return F.freeze(self.source, require_git=False, commit_override=COMMIT,
+                        tree_override=TREE, repo_url_override="FIXTURE_NO_NETWORK")
+
+    def manifest(self, **overrides) -> dict:
+        doc = {
+            "schema": B.MANIFEST_SCHEMA_ID,
+            "plugin_id": PLUGIN_ID,
+            "display_name": "PIPD Fixture Public Skills",
+            "version": "0.1.1",
+            "license": "Apache-2.0",
+            "skills": list(SKILLS),
+            "official_schema_sha256": sha256(self.schema_bytes),
+            "publisher": {
+                "name": "PIPD Owner",
+                "identity": "owner@example.invalid",
+                "identity_sha256": "f" * 64,
+            },
+            "icons": [{"path": "assets/icon-128.png", "sha256": sha256(self.icon_bytes),
+                       "size": 128}],
+            "release": {"claim_ceiling": "LOCAL_PACKAGER_PASS_ONLY",
+                        "official_portal_verification": "NOT_EXECUTED"},
+        }
+        doc.update(overrides)
+        return doc
+
+    def write_packaging(self, ledger: dict, *, manifest: dict | None = None,
+                        derivations: dict | None = None) -> None:
+        doc = manifest if manifest is not None else self.manifest()
+        (self.packaging / "plugin.json").write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(doc))
+        deriv = derivations if derivations is not None else derivations_doc(ledger)
+        (self.packaging / "derivations.json").write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(deriv))
+
+    def write_ledger(self, ledger: dict) -> Path:
+        path = self.root / "ledger.json"
+        path.write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(ledger))
+        return path
+
+    def build(self, ledger: dict, *, source_commit: str | None = COMMIT, **kwargs):
+        return B.build_plugin(source_root=self.source, ledger=ledger, source_commit=source_commit,
+                              packaging_root=self.packaging, out_dir=self.out, **kwargs)
+
+
+def derivation_record(ledger: dict, name: str, **overrides) -> dict:
+    rel = f"skills/{name}/SKILL.md"
+    record = {
+        "skill": name,
+        "source_path": rel,
+        "source_sha256": ledger["files"][rel],
+        "kept_keys": list(APPROVED_KEYS),
+        "dropped_keys": list(DROPPED_KEYS),
+        "approved_by": "owner@example.invalid",
+        "approval_receipt": "owner-approval-receipt-20261012-0001",
+    }
+    record.update(overrides)
+    return record
+
+
+def derivations_doc(ledger: dict, *, overrides: dict[str, dict] | None = None) -> dict:
+    overrides = overrides or {}
+    return {
+        "schema": "PIPD-PUBLIC-PLUGIN-DERIVATIONS/1",
+        "derivations": [derivation_record(ledger, name, **overrides.get(name, {}))
+                        for name in sorted(SKILLS)],
+    }
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def temp_env():
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+        yield Env(Path(tmp))
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def as_symlink(path: Path, target: Path):
+    """Present ``path`` as a symlink to ``target``; fall back to the documented seam.
+
+    The seam (``build_public_plugin._path_is_symlink``) exists precisely so the symlink gates can
+    be exercised on hosts that forbid real symlinks. Only the predicate is substituted; every
+    other line of the gate is the real, unmodified code.
+    """
+    try:
+        os.symlink(target, path, target_is_directory=target.is_dir())
+    except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
+        real = B._path_is_symlink
+        wanted = Path(path)
+
+        def fake(candidate, _wanted=wanted, _real=real):
+            try:
+                if Path(candidate) == _wanted:
+                    return True
+            except TypeError:
+                pass
+            return _real(candidate)
+
+        B._path_is_symlink = fake
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            B._path_is_symlink = real
+    else:
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            try:
+                path.unlink()
+            except OSError:
+                pass
+
+
+def zip_entries(path: Path) -> tuple[list[zipfile.ZipInfo], dict[str, bytes]]:
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
+        infos = archive.infolist()
+        members = {info.filename: archive.read(info.filename) for info in infos}
+    return infos, members
+
+
+class PublicPluginPackagingTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
+    def assert_refusal(self, code: str, func, *args, **kwargs) -> B.Refusal:
+        with self.assertRaises(B.Refusal) as caught:
+            func(*args, **kwargs)
+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, code, str(caught.exception))
+        return caught.exception
+
+    def assert_no_zip(self, env: Env) -> None:
+        if env.out.exists():
+            self.assertEqual([p.name for p in env.out.iterdir()], [],
+                             "a refused build must not leave anything behind")
+
+    def run_git(self, repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
+        proc = subprocess.run(
+            [GIT, "-C", str(repo), "-c", "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
+             "-c", "user.name=packaging-fixture", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false",
+             "-c", "init.defaultBranch=main", *args],
+            capture_output=True, text=True)
+        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr or proc.stdout)
+        return proc.stdout
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------- 0. the schema subset
+    def test_00_local_schema_is_a_locally_authored_subset(self) -> None:
+        doc = json.loads(SCHEMA_PATH.read_bytes().decode("utf-8"))
+        self.assertEqual(doc["$schema"], "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema")
+        self.assertIs(doc["additionalProperties"], False)
+        description = doc["description"].upper()
+        self.assertIn("LOCALLY AUTHORED SUBSET", description)
+        self.assertIn("NOT THE OFFICIAL VENDOR SCHEMA", description)
+        self.assertIn("NOT_EXECUTED", description)
+        self.assertEqual(sorted(doc["properties"]), sorted([
+            "schema", "plugin_id", "display_name", "version", "license", "skills",
+            "official_schema_sha256", "publisher", "icons", "release"]))
+        # The builder's own validator consumes the subset and accepts the checked-in manifest...
+        manifest = json.loads(CHECKED_IN_MANIFEST.read_bytes().decode("utf-8"))
+        self.assertEqual(B.validate_subset(manifest, doc), [])
+        # ... rejects an unknown key, a ninth skill, and a non-enum skill name.
+        self.assertTrue(B.validate_subset({**manifest, "custom": 1}, doc))
+        extra = json.loads(json.dumps(manifest))
+        extra["skills"] = list(SKILLS) + ["pipd-extra-skill"]
+        self.assertTrue(B.validate_subset(extra, doc))
+        renamed = json.loads(json.dumps(manifest))
+        renamed["skills"] = ["pipd-not-a-skill"] + list(SKILLS)[1:]
+        self.assertTrue(B.validate_subset(renamed, doc))
+
+    # --------------------------------------------------------- 1. broken icon data
+    def test_01_png_signature_with_broken_body_is_refused(self) -> None:
+        fake = B.PNG_SIG + b"garbage-body"
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            (env.assets / "icon-128.png").write_bytes(fake)
+            env.write_packaging(ledger, manifest=env.manifest(icons=[
+                {"path": "assets/icon-128.png", "sha256": sha256(fake), "size": 128}]))
+            exc = self.assert_refusal("ICON_INVALID", env.build, ledger)
+            self.assertIn("truncated_chunk", str(exc))
+            self.assert_no_zip(env)
+
+    def test_01_non_png_icon_is_refused(self) -> None:
+        fake = b"GIF89a this is not a png file\n"
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            (env.assets / "icon-128.png").write_bytes(fake)
+            env.write_packaging(ledger, manifest=env.manifest(icons=[
+                {"path": "assets/icon-128.png", "sha256": sha256(fake), "size": 128}]))
+            exc = self.assert_refusal("ICON_INVALID", env.build, ledger)
+            self.assertIn("signature", str(exc))
+            self.assert_no_zip(env)

+    def test_04_source_commit_gates(self) -> None:
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            env.write_packaging(ledger)
+            self.assert_refusal("SOURCE_COMMIT_NULL", env.build, ledger, source_commit=None)
+            self.assert_refusal("SOURCE_COMMIT_INVALID", env.build, ledger, source_commit="abc123")
+            self.assert_refusal("SOURCE_COMMIT_MISMATCH", env.build, ledger, source_commit="e" * 40)
+            self.assert_no_zip(env)

+    # ------------------------------------------------- 5. symlinked output release
+    def test_05_symlinked_output_root_is_refused_and_target_untouched(self) -> None:
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            env.write_packaging(ledger)
+            target = env.root / "release-target"
+            target.mkdir()
+            sentinel = target / "SENTINEL.txt"
+            sentinel_bytes = b"sentinel bytes that must survive untouched\n"
+            sentinel.write_bytes(sentinel_bytes)
+            link = env.root / "release-link"
+            with as_symlink(link, target):
+                env.out = link
+                self.assert_refusal("OUTPUT_ROOT_SYMLINK", env.build, ledger)
+            self.assertEqual(sentinel.read_bytes(), sentinel_bytes)
+            self.assertEqual(sorted(p.name for p in target.iterdir()), ["SENTINEL.txt"])

+    def test_08_non_regular_source_member_is_refused(self) -> None:
+        # A non-directory entry where a skill pack is expected.
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            env.write_packaging(ledger)
+            (env.skills / "STRAY_MEMBER.txt").write_text(
+                "not a skill directory\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="")

+            self.assertIn("STRAY_MEMBER.txt", str(exc))
+            self.assert_no_zip(env)
+        if hasattr(os, "mkfifo"):
+            # POSIX only: a FIFO inside a skill is a non-regular source member.
+            with temp_env() as env:
+                ledger = env.freeze()
+                env.write_packaging(ledger)
+                os.mkfifo(env.skills / "pipd-pd-bind" / "pipe")
+                exc = self.assert_refusal("SOURCE_SPECIAL_MEMBER", env.build, ledger)
+                self.assertIn("pipe", str(exc))

+    # ------------------------------------------------------- 9. dirty worktree freeze
+    @unittest.skipUnless(GIT, "git is required to exercise the real freeze() git gates")
+    def test_09_dirty_worktree_at_freeze_time_is_refused(self) -> None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp) / "repo"
+            repo.mkdir()
+            self.run_git(repo, "init", "--quiet")
+            (repo / "UNTRACKED.txt").write_text("uncommitted\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            with self.assertRaises(F.FreezeRefusal) as caught:
+                F.freeze(repo)

+            self.assertIn("UNTRACKED.txt", str(caught.exception))

+    # --------------------------------------------------------- 10. determinism
+    def test_10_two_builds_are_byte_identical(self) -> None:
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            env.write_packaging(ledger)
+            first = env.build(ledger)
+            first_zip = Path(first["out_zip"])
+            first_bytes = first_zip.read_bytes()
+            first_infos, first_members = zip_entries(first_zip)
+
+            second = B.build_plugin(source_root=env.source, ledger=ledger, source_commit=COMMIT,
+                                    packaging_root=env.packaging, out_dir=env.root / "release-2")
+            second_zip = Path(second["out_zip"])
+            second_bytes = second_zip.read_bytes()
+            second_infos, second_members = zip_entries(second_zip)
+
+            self.assertEqual(sha256(first_bytes), first["zip_sha256"])
+            self.assertEqual(first_bytes, second_bytes)
+            self.assertEqual(sha256(first_bytes), sha256(second_bytes))
+            self.assertEqual(first_members, second_members)
+            self.assertEqual([i.filename for i in first_infos],
+                             [i.filename for i in second_infos])
+            self.assertEqual([i.filename for i in first_infos], sorted(first_members))
+            for info in first_infos:
+                self.assertEqual(info.date_time, FIXED_DATE_TIME)
+                self.assertEqual(info.external_attr >> 16, FIXED_MODE)
+                self.assertEqual(info.compress_type, zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)
+
+    # ------------------------------------- 11. missing owner record -> non-zero exit
+    def test_11_missing_owner_derivation_is_a_non_zero_exit(self) -> None:
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            env.write_packaging(ledger, derivations={
+                "schema": "PIPD-PUBLIC-PLUGIN-DERIVATIONS/1", "derivations": []})
+            ledger_path = env.write_ledger(ledger)
+            captured = io.StringIO()
+            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(captured):
+                code = B.main(["--source-root", str(env.source), "--ledger", str(ledger_path),
+                               "--source-commit", COMMIT, "--packaging-root", str(env.packaging),
+                               "--out-dir", str(env.out)])
+            printed = captured.getvalue().strip()
+            self.assertEqual(printed,
+                             "REFUSED OWNER_INPUT_MISSING: "
+                             + B.DERIVATION_MISSING_TEMPLATE.format(skill="pipd-assurance-tqaep"))
+            self.assertEqual(code, 2)
+            self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)
+            self.assert_no_zip(env)

+    # ------------------------------------------ 12. complete record -> verbatim body
+    def test_12_complete_owner_record_builds_and_projects_the_body_verbatim(self) -> None:
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            env.write_packaging(ledger)
+            report = env.build(ledger)
+            self.assertEqual(report["verdict"], "BUILT")
+            infos, members = zip_entries(Path(report["out_zip"]))
+            root = PLUGIN_ID
+
+            mapping = json.loads(members[f"{root}/SOURCE_TO_PLUGIN_MAPPING.json"].decode("utf-8"))
+            receipt = json.loads(members[f"{root}/RELEASE_RECEIPT.json"].decode("utf-8"))
+            self.assertEqual(receipt["claim_ceiling"], "LOCAL_PACKAGER_PASS_ONLY")
+            self.assertEqual(receipt["official_portal_verification"], "NOT_EXECUTED")
+            rows = {row["source_path"]: row for row in mapping["entries"]}
+
+            for name in SKILLS:
+                rel = f"skills/{name}/SKILL.md"
+                row = rows[rel]
+                self.assertEqual(row["mode"], "DERIVED_WITH_OWNER_APPROVAL")
+                self.assertEqual(row["destination_path"], f"{root}/{rel}")
+                self.assertEqual(row["source_sha256"], ledger["files"][rel])
+
+                source_bytes = F.canonical_bytes((env.skills / name / "SKILL.md").read_bytes())
+                _, source_map, source_body = B.parse_skill_md(source_bytes.decode("utf-8"))
+                projected = members[f"{root}/{rel}"]
+                _, projected_map, projected_body = B.parse_skill_md(projected.decode("utf-8"))
+
+                # The body survives the projection byte-for-byte; only approved keys move.
+                self.assertEqual(projected_body, source_body)
+                self.assertEqual(set(projected_map), set(APPROVED_KEYS))
+                for key in APPROVED_KEYS:
+                    self.assertEqual(projected_map[key], source_map[key])
+                for key in DROPPED_KEYS:
+                    self.assertNotIn(key, projected_map)
+                self.assertEqual(row["destination_sha256"], sha256(projected))
+
+            self.assertEqual(members[f"{root}/plugin.schema.json"], env.schema_bytes)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------- 13. output root overlap / dist
+    def test_13_output_root_overlapping_the_repo_or_dist_is_refused(self) -> None:
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            env.write_packaging(ledger)
+            cases = (
+                (env.source, "OUTPUT_ROOT_OVERLAPS_REPO"),
+                (env.source / "candidate", "OUTPUT_ROOT_OVERLAPS_REPO"),
+                (env.root, "OUTPUT_ROOT_OVERLAPS_REPO"),
+                (env.source / "dist", "OUTPUT_ROOT_IN_DIST"),
+                (env.source / "dist" / "nested", "OUTPUT_ROOT_IN_DIST"),
+            )
+            for out_dir, code in cases:
+                with self.subTest(out_dir=str(out_dir)):
+                    call = functools.partial(
+                        B.build_plugin, source_root=env.source, ledger=ledger,
+                        source_commit=COMMIT, packaging_root=env.packaging, out_dir=out_dir)
+                    self.assert_refusal(code, call)
+            self.assertFalse((env.source / "dist").exists())

+    # --------------------------------------------- 14. owner placeholders refuse
+    def test_14_owner_placeholders_are_refused(self) -> None:
+        with temp_env() as env:
+            ledger = env.freeze()
+            env.write_packaging(ledger, manifest=env.manifest(
+                official_schema_sha256="OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED"))
+            self.assert_refusal("OWNER_INPUT_MISSING", env.build, ledger)
+
+            env.write_packaging(ledger, manifest=env.manifest(publisher={
+                "name": "OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED",

+"""Packaging tests for the public Skills-only plugin builder and source freezer.
+
+These tests pin the fail-closed contract of ``tools/build_public_plugin.py`` and
+``tools/freeze_public_plugin_source.py``. Every case drives the REAL ``build_plugin(...)`` /
+``freeze(...)`` functions (never a re-implementation) and every case runs inside a private
+temporary directory: no network, no writes into the repository, nothing under ``dist/`` or
+``.hgk/``.
+
+They are also the historical red cases: they were written against the defect where the builder
+accepted a ``SKILL.md`` whose frontmatter ``name`` did not match its skill directory (the tool is
+fixed here, in ``project_skill_md``), and they pin the digest-pinnable, locally authored
+``plugin.schema.json`` subset that the builder validates the manifest with.
+
+Symlinks are exercised through the documented ``build_public_plugin._path_is_symlink`` seam when
+the host refuses to create a real symlink (unprivileged Windows), so the gate itself is always
+executed; where the OS allows the real thing, the real thing is used.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import functools
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+TOOLS = ROOT / "tools"
+if str(TOOLS) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS))
+
+import build_public_plugin as B  # noqa: E402  (sibling tool, stdlib-only)
+import freeze_public_plugin_source as F  # noqa: E402  (sibling tool, stdlib-only)
+
+SCHEMA_PATH = ROOT / "packaging" / "public-plugin" / "plugin.schema.json"
+CHECKED_IN_MANIFEST = ROOT / "packaging" / "public-plugin" / "plugin.json"
+GIT = shutil.which("git")
+
+COMMIT = "c" * 40
+TREE = "d" * 40
+PLUGIN_ID = "pipd-ls-sp-public-skills"
+SKILLS = tuple(F.EXPECTED_SKILLS)
+
+# The fixture frontmatter carries both portable and non-portable keys, exactly like the real packs.
+APPROVED_KEYS = ("name", "description", "license")
+DROPPED_KEYS = ("version", "owner", "triggers", "schemas", "references", "tests")
+
+FIXED_DATE_TIME = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
+FIXED_MODE = 0o644
+
+
+def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def skill_md_text(name: str, *, declared_name: str | None = None) -> str:
+    declared = name if declared_name is None else declared_name
+    return (
+        "---\n"
+        f"name: {declared}\n"
+        "description: Fixture skill for the public plugin packaging tests.\n"
+        "license: Apache-2.0\n"
+        "version: 1\n"
+        "owner: PIPD-EC (deterministic compiler)\n"
+        "triggers:\n"
+        "  - fixture trigger\n"
+        "schemas:\n"
+        "  - schemas/input.schema.json\n"
+        "references:\n"
+        "  - references/contract.md\n"
+        "tests:\n"
+        "  - tests/cases.yaml\n"
+        "---\n"
+        "\n"
+        f"# {name}\n"
+        "\n"
+        "## Contract (imperative)\n"
+        "\n"
+        "1. Keep the body byte-identical across the frontmatter projection.\n"
+        "2. Never let a packaging run touch a real repository tree.\n"
+    )
+
+
+class Env:
+    """A throwaway source checkout + packaging root, entirely under one temp directory."""
+
+    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
+        self.root = root
+        self.source = root / "source"
+        self.skills = self.source / "skills"
+        self.packaging = root / "packaging"
+        self.assets = self.packaging / "assets"
+        self.out = root / "release"
+        for name in SKILLS:
+            skill_dir = self.skills / name
+            skill_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            (skill_dir / "SKILL.md").write_text(skill_md_text(name), encoding="utf-8", newline="")
+        self.assets.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        # The real, checked-in local schema subset is what the builder must consume.
+        shutil.copyfile(SCHEMA_PATH, self.packaging / "plugin.schema.json")
+        (self.assets / "icon-128.png").write_bytes(B.png_icon_bytes(128))
+
+    @property
+    def schema_bytes(self) -> bytes:
+        return (self.packaging / "plugin.schema.json").read_bytes()
+
+    @property
+    def icon_bytes(self) -> bytes:
+        return (self.assets / "icon-128.png").read_bytes()
+
+    def freeze(self) -> dict:
+        return F.freeze(self.source, require_git=False, commit_override=COMMIT,
+                        tree_override=TREE, repo_url_override="FIXTURE_NO_NETWORK")
+
+    def manifest(self, **overrides) -> dict:
+        doc = {
+            "schema": B.MANIFEST_SCHEMA_ID,
+            "plugin_id": PLUGIN_ID,
+            "display_name": "PIPD Fixture Public Skills",
+            "version": "0.1.1",
+            "license": "Apache-2.0",
+            "skills": list(SKILLS),
+            "official_schema_sha256": sha256(self.schema_bytes),
+            "publisher": {
+                "name": "PIPD Owner",
+                "identity": "owner@example.invalid",
+                "identity_sha256": "f" * 64,
+            },
+            "icons": [{"path": "assets/icon-128.png", "sha256": sha256(self.icon_bytes),
+                       "size": 128}],
+            "release": {"claim_ceiling": "LOCAL_PACKAGER_PASS_ONLY",
+                        "official_portal_verification": "NOT_EXECUTED"},
+        }
+        doc.update(overrides)
+        return doc
+
+    def write_packaging(self, ledger: dict, *, manifest: dict | None = None,
+                        derivations: dict | None = None) -> None:
+        doc = manifest if manifest is not None else self.manifest()
+        (self.packaging / "plugin.json").write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(doc))
+        deriv = derivations if derivations is not None else derivations_doc(ledger)
+        (self.packaging / "derivations.json").write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(deriv))
+
+    def write_ledger(self, ledger: dict) -> Path:
+        path = self.root / "ledger.json"
+        path.write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(ledger))
+        return path
+
+    def build(self, ledger: dict, *, source_commit: str | None = COMMIT, **kwargs):
+        return B.build_plugin(source_root=self.source, ledger=ledger, source_commit=source_commit,
+                              packaging_root=self.packaging, out_dir=self.out, **kwargs)
+
+
+def derivation_record(ledger: dict, name: str, **overrides) -> dict:
+    rel = f"skills/{name}/SKILL.md"
+    record = {
+        "skill": name,
+        "source_path": rel,
+        "source_sha256": ledger["files"][rel],
+        "kept_keys": list(APPROVED_KEYS),
+        "dropped_keys": list(DROPPED_KEYS),
+        "approved_by": "owner@example.invalid",
+        "approval_receipt": "owner-approval-receipt-20261012-0001",
+    }
+    record.update(overrides)
+    return record
+
+
+def derivations_doc(ledger: dict, *, overrides: dict[str, dict] | None = None) -> dict:
+    overrides = overrides or {}
+    return {
+        "schema": "PIPD-PUBLIC-PLUGIN-DERIVATIONS/1",
+        "derivations": [derivation_record(ledger, name, **overrides.get(name, {}))
+                        for name in sorted(SKILLS)],
+    }
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def temp_env():
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+        yield Env(Path(tmp))
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def as_symlink(path: Path, target: Path):
+    """Present ``path`` as a symlink to ``target``; fall back to the documented seam.
+
+    The seam (``build_public_plugin._path_is_symlink``) exists precisely so the symlink gates can
+    be exercised on hosts that forbid real symlinks. Only the predicate is substituted; every
+    other line of the gate is the real, unmodified code.
+    """
+    try:
+        os.symlink(target, path, target_is_directory=target.is_dir())
+    except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
+        real = B._path_is_symlink
+        wanted = Path(path)
+
+        def fake(candidate, _wanted=wanted, _real=real):
+            try:
+                if Path(candidate) == _wanted:
+                    return True
+            except TypeError:
+                pass
+            return _real(candidate)
+
+        B._path_is_symlink = fake
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            B._path_is_symlink = real
+    else:
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            try:
+                path.unlink()
+            except OSError:
+                pass
+
+
+def zip_entries(path: Path) -> tuple[list[zipfile.ZipInfo], dict[str, bytes]]:
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
+        infos = archive.infolist()
+        members = {info.filename: archive.read(info.filename) for info in infos}
+    return infos, members
+
+
+class PublicPluginPackagingTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
+    def assert_refusal(self, code: str, func, *args, **kwargs) -> B.Refusal:
+        with self.assertRaises(B.Refusal) as caught:
+            func(*args, **kwargs)
+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, code, str(caught.exception))
+        return caught.exception
+
+    def assert_no_zip(self, env: Env) -> None:
+        if env.out.exists():
+            self.assertEqual([p.name for p in env.out.iterdir()], [],
+                             "a refused build must not leave anything behind")
+
+    def run_git(self, repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
+        proc = subprocess.run(
+            [GIT, "-C", str(repo), "-c", "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
+             "-c", "user.name=packaging-fixture", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false",
+             "-c", "init.defaultBranch=main", *args],
+            capture_output=True, text=True)
+        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr or proc.stdout)
+        return proc.stdout
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------- 0. the schema subset
+    def test_00_local_schema_is_a_locally_authored_subset(self) -> None:
+        doc = json.loads(SCHEMA_PATH.read_bytes().decode("utf-8"))
+        self.assertEqual(doc["$schema"], "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema")
+        self.assertIs(doc["additionalProperties"], False)
+        description = doc["description"].upper()
+        self.assertIn("LOCALLY AUTHORED SUBSET", description)
+        self.assertIn("NOT THE OFFICIAL VENDOR SCHEMA", description)
+        self.assertIn("NOT_EXECUTED", description)
+        self.assertEqual(sorted(doc["properties"]), sorted([
+            "schema", "plugin_id", "display_name", "version", "license", "skills",
+            "official_schema_sha256", "publisher", "icons", "release"]))
+        # The builder's own validator consumes the subset and accepts the checked-in manifest...
+        manifest = json.loads(CHECKED_IN_MANIFEST.read_bytes().decode("utf-8"))
+        self.assertEqual(B.validate_subset(manifest, doc), [])
+        # ... rejects an unknown key, a ninth skill, and a non-enum skill name.
+        self.assertTrue(B.validate_subset({**manifest, "custom": 1}, doc))
+        extra = json.loads(json.dumps(manifest))
+        extra["skills"] = list(SKILLS) + ["pipd-extra-skill"]
+        self.assertTrue(B.validate_subset(extra, doc))
+        renamed = json.loads(json.dumps(manifest))
+        renamed["skills"] = ["pipd-not-a-skill"] + list(SKILLS)[1:]
+        self.assertTrue(B.validate_subset(renamed, doc))
+
+    # --------------------------------------------------------- 1. broken icon data
+    def test_01_png_signature_with_broken_body_is_refused(self) -> None:

+            self.assertIn("truncated_chunk", str(exc))
+            self.assert_no_zip(env)
+
+    def test_01_non_png_icon_is_refused(self) -> None:

+            ledger = env.freeze()

+                {"path": "assets/icon-128.png", "sha256": sha256(fake), "size": 128}]))
+            exc = self.assert_refusal("ICON_INVALID", env.build, ledger)

+            self.assert_no_zip(env)

codex
Both deliverables are in place, the tool fix is confined to the one proven defect, and the whole suite is green. Summary of what I did:

**Changed files (all inside the allowed write set)**
- `packaging/public-plugin/plugin.schema.json` (new) — draft 2020-12 **locally authored subset** mirroring exactly the builder's manifest constraints: the ten top-level keys, `additionalProperties: false` at every level, `schema` const, `skills` pinned to the eight exact names (8 items, unique, enum), publisher/icon objects with required fields, `release` shape. Its `description` states it is a LOCALLY AUTHORED SUBSET, that it is NOT the official vendor schema, and that the vendor schema/validator remain `NOT_EXECUTED`. Its bytes are digest-pinnable via `official_schema_sha256`.
- `tests/test_public_plugin_packaging.py` (new) — 19 stdlib `unittest` cases, temp-dir fixtures, no network, never touching the real tree, all driving the real `build_plugin(...)`/`freeze(...)` (and `main()` for the exit-code case). Symlink cases use the documented `_path_is_symlink` seam only when the host refuses real symlinks, so the real gate code always runs.
- `tools/build_public_plugin.py` — one proven defect fixed: `project_skill_md` never checked that the frontmatter `name` matches the skill directory, so case 3 ("wrong `name`") was not refused. It now raises `SKILL_FRONTMATTER_INVALID`. No other behavior changed.

*(Note: `tools/build_web_fallback.py` / `tests/test_web_fallback.py` show as modified/untracked in `git status` — they were changed by a concurrent lane, not by me; they are on the forbidden list and untouched by this lane.)*

+"""Packaging tests for the public Skills-only plugin builder and source freezer.
+
+These tests pin the fail-closed contract of ``tools/build_public_plugin.py`` and
+``tools/freeze_public_plugin_source.py``. Every case drives the REAL ``build_plugin(...)`` /
+``freeze(...)`` functions (never a re-implementation) and every case runs inside a private
+temporary directory: no network, no writes into the repository, nothing under ``dist/`` or
+``.hgk/``.
+
+They are also the historical red cases: they were written against the defect where the builder
+accepted a ``SKILL.md`` whose frontmatter ``name`` did not match its skill directory (the tool is
+fixed here, in ``project_skill_md``), and they pin the digest-pinnable, locally authored
+``plugin.schema.json`` subset that the builder validates the manifest with.
+
+Symlinks are exercised through the documented ``build_public_plugin._path_is_symlink`` seam when
+the host refuses to create a real symlink (unprivileged Windows), so the gate itself is always
+executed; where the OS allows the real thing, the real thing is used.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import functools
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+TOOLS = ROOT / "tools"
+if str(TOOLS) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS))
+
+import build_public_plugin as B  # noqa: E402  (sibling tool, stdlib-only)
+import freeze_public_plugin_source as F  # noqa: E402  (sibling tool, stdlib-only)
+
+SCHEMA_PATH = ROOT / "packaging" / "public-plugin" / "plugin.schema.json"
+CHECKED_IN_MANIFEST = ROOT / "packaging" / "public-plugin" / "plugin.json"
+GIT = shutil.which("git")
+
+COMMIT = "c" * 40
+TREE = "d" * 40
+PLUGIN_ID = "pipd-ls-sp-public-skills"
+SKILLS = tuple(F.EXPECTED_SKILLS)
+
+# The fixture frontmatter carries both portable and non-portable keys, exactly like the real packs.
+APPROVED_KEYS = ("name", "description", "license")
+DROPPED_KEYS = ("version", "owner", "triggers", "schemas", "references", "tests")
+
+FIXED_DATE_TIME = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
+FIXED_MODE = 0o644
+
+
+def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def skill_md_text(name: str, *, declared_name: str | None = None) -> str:
+    declared = name if declared_name is None else declared_name
+    return (
+        "---\n"
+        f"name: {declared}\n"
+        "description: Fixture skill for the public plugin packaging tests.\n"
+        "license: Apache-2.0\n"
+        "version: 1\n"
+        "owner: PIPD-EC (deterministic compiler)\n"
+        "triggers:\n"
+        "  - fixture trigger\n"
+        "schemas:\n"
+        "  - schemas/input.schema.json\n"
+        "references:\n"
+        "  - references/contract.md\n"
+        "tests:\n"
+        "  - tests/cases.yaml\n"
+        "---\n"
+        "\n"
+        f"# {name}\n"
+        "\n"
+        "## Contract (imperative)\n"
+        "\n"
+        "1. Keep the body byte-identical across the frontmatter projection.\n"
+        "2. Never let a packaging run touch a real repository tree.\n"
+    )
+
+
+class Env:
+    """A throwaway source checkout + packaging root, entirely under one temp directory."""
+
+    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
+        self.root = root
+        self.source = root / "source"
+        self.skills = self.source / "skills"
+        self.packaging = root / "packaging"
+        self.assets = self.packaging / "assets"
+        self.out = root / "release"
+        for name in SKILLS:
+            skill_dir = self.skills / name
+            skill_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            (skill_dir / "SKILL.md").write_text(skill_md_text(name), encoding="utf-8", newline="")
+        self.assets.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        # The real, checked-in local schema subset is what the builder must consume.
+        shutil.copyfile(SCHEMA_PATH, self.packaging / "plugin.schema.json")
+        (self.assets / "icon-128.png").write_bytes(B.png_icon_bytes(128))
+
+    @property
+    def schema_bytes(self) -> bytes:
+        return (self.packaging / "plugin.schema.json").read_bytes()
+
+    @property
+    def icon_bytes(self) -> bytes:
+        return (self.assets / "icon-128.png").read_bytes()
+
+    def freeze(self) -> dict:
+        return F.freeze(self.source, require_git=False, commit_override=COMMIT,
+                        tree_override=TREE, repo_url_override="FIXTURE_NO_NETWORK")
+
+    def manifest(self, **overrides) -> dict:
+        doc = {
+            "schema": B.MANIFEST_SCHEMA_ID,
+            "plugin_id": PLUGIN_ID,
+            "display_name": "PIPD Fixture Public Skills",
+            "version": "0.1.1",
+            "license": "Apache-2.0",
+            "skills": list(SKILLS),
+            "official_schema_sha256": sha256(self.schema_bytes),
+            "publisher": {
+                "name": "PIPD Owner",
+                "identity": "owner@example.invalid",
+                "identity_sha256": "f" * 64,
+            },
+            "icons": [{"path": "assets/icon-128.png", "sha256": sha256(self.icon_bytes),
+                       "size": 128}],
+            "release": {"claim_ceiling": "LOCAL_PACKAGER_PASS_ONLY",
+                        "official_portal_verification": "NOT_EXECUTED"},
+        }
+        doc.update(overrides)
+        return doc
+
+    def write_packaging(self, ledger: dict, *, manifest: dict | None = None,
+                        derivations: dict | None = None) -> None:
+        doc = manifest if manifest is not None else self.manifest()
+        (self.packaging / "plugin.json").write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(doc))
+        deriv = derivations if derivations is not None else derivations_doc(ledger)
+        (self.packaging / "derivations.json").write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(deriv))
+
+    def write_ledger(self, ledger: dict) -> Path:
+        path = self.root / "ledger.json"
+        path.write_bytes(B.canonical_json_bytes(ledger))
+        return path
+
+    def build(self, ledger: dict, *, source_commit: str | None = COMMIT, **kwargs):
+        return B.build_plugin(source_root=self.source, ledger=ledger, source_commit=source_commit,
+                              packaging_root=self.packaging, out_dir=self.out, **kwargs)
+
+
+def derivation_record(ledger: dict, name: str, **overrides) -> dict:
+    rel = f"skills/{name}/SKILL.md"
+    record = {
+        "skill": name,
+        "source_path": rel,
+        "source_sha256": ledger["files"][rel],
+        "kept_keys": list(APPROVED_KEYS),
+        "dropped_keys": list(DROPPED_KEYS),
+        "approved_by": "owner@example.invalid",
+        "approval_receipt": "owner-approval-receipt-20261012-0001",
+    }
+    record.update(overrides)
+    return record
+
+
+def derivations_doc(ledger: dict, *, overrides: dict[str, dict] | None = None) -> dict:
+    overrides = overrides or {}
+    return {
+        "schema": "PIPD-PUBLIC-PLUGIN-DERIVATIONS/1",
+        "derivations": [derivation_record(ledger, name, **overrides.get(name, {}))
+                        for name in sorted(SKILLS)],
+    }
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def temp_env():
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+        yield Env(Path(tmp))
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def as_symlink(path: Path, target: Path):
+    """Present ``path`` as a symlink to ``target``; fall back to the documented seam.
+
+    The seam (``build_public_plugin._path_is_symlink``) exists precisely so the symlink gates can
+    be exercised on hosts that forbid real symlinks. Only the predicate is substituted; every
+    other line of the gate is the real, unmodified code.
+    """
+    try:
+        os.symlink(target, path, target_is_directory=target.is_dir())
+    except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
+        real = B._path_is_symlink
+        wanted = Path(path)
+
+        def fake(candidate, _wanted=wanted, _real=real):
+            try:
+                if Path(candidate) == _wanted:
+                    return True
+            except TypeError:
+                pass
+            return _real(candidate)
+
+        B._path_is_symlink = fake
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            B._path_is_symlink = real
+    else:
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            try:
+                path.unlink()
+            except OSError:
+                pass
+
+
+def zip_entries(path: Path) -> tuple[list[zipfile.ZipInfo], dict[str, bytes]]:
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
+        infos = archive.infolist()
+        members = {info.filename: archive.read(info.filename) for info in infos}
+    return infos, members
+
+

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""S4POST Stage B: project one frozen Web mount pack into ONE bounded fallback document.

There is no public directory listing for the plugin yet, so the current Web route is a single
markdown document a reader can attach to a conversation or a Knowledge base. This tool builds that
document from a *frozen mount pack* (a directory carrying ``MANIFEST.sha256``) and is fail-closed:
it REFUSES (typed reason, non-zero exit) rather than warn on

  * ``MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH``  a member's bytes no longer match ``MANIFEST.sha256``
  * ``MEMBER_SYMLINK``            a symlinked member (or pack) is present
  * ``PATH_ESCAPE``               a manifest path escapes the pack root
  * ``UNEXPECTED_EXTRA_FILE``     a file exists in the pack that the manifest does not list
  * ``RELEASE_STAMP_MISSING``     a member document does not stamp the release commit
  * ``SIZE_CAP_EXCEEDED``         the composed document would exceed the cap (NEVER truncated)
  * ``DESTINATION_EXISTS`` / ``DESTINATION_SYMLINK``  the output file already exists

The document is written with ``O_EXCL`` and stamps ``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY`` plus the member inventory. No
timestamp is embedded, so two builds are byte-identical.

CLI
---
``--mount-pack DIR``      unpacked frozen mount pack (contains MANIFEST.sha256)
``--release-id TEXT``     e.g. v0.1.1-preview.3 (informational stamp)
``--release-commit HEX40`` the commit the members must stamp
``--size-cap BYTES``      hard cap for the composed document (default 524288)
``--out FILE``            destination markdown file (must not exist)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MANIFEST_NAME = "MANIFEST.sha256"
FALLBACK_SCHEMA = "PIPD-WEB-FALLBACK/1"
DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP = 524288
HEX40 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")


class Refusal(Exception):
    """A fail-closed refusal. ``code`` is the machine-checkable typed reason."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"REFUSED {code}: {detail}")
        self.code = code
        self.detail = detail


def _path_is_symlink(path) -> bool:
    """Seam for tests: a single predicate the destination gate consults."""
    return os.path.islink(path)


def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _canonical_bytes(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if b"\x00" in data:
        return data
    try:
        data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return data
    return data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n").replace(b"\r", b"\n")


def _parse_manifest(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    entries: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if "  " not in line:
            raise Refusal("MANIFEST_INVALID", f"line has no two-space separator: {line!r}")
        digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
        digest, rel = digest.strip(), rel.strip()
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", digest):
            raise Refusal("MANIFEST_INVALID", f"digest is not 64 hex chars: {digest!r}")
        entries.append((digest, rel))
    if not entries:
        raise Refusal("MANIFEST_INVALID", "MANIFEST.sha256 lists no members")
    return entries


def _escapes(rel: str) -> bool:
    parts = rel.replace("\\", "/").split("/")
    return (rel.startswith("/") or "\\" in rel or ":" in rel or ".." in parts
            or any(part == "" for part in parts) or parts[0] in (".", ""))


def load_and_verify_pack(mount_pack: Path, release_commit: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, bytes]]:
    """Return [(rel, sha256, bytes), ...] for a verified, exactly-listed pack."""
    mount_pack = Path(mount_pack)
    if _path_is_symlink(mount_pack):
        raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", f"mount pack {mount_pack} is a symlink")
    if not mount_pack.is_dir():
        raise Refusal("MOUNT_PACK_MISSING", f"mount pack is not a directory: {mount_pack}")
    manifest_path = mount_pack / MANIFEST_NAME
    if _path_is_symlink(manifest_path):
        raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", f"{manifest_path} is a symlink")
    if not manifest_path.is_file():
        raise Refusal("MANIFEST_MISSING", f"{manifest_path} is absent")
    entries = _parse_manifest(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    listed: list[tuple[str, str, bytes]] = []
    listed_paths: set[str] = set()
    for digest, rel in entries:
        if _escapes(rel):
            raise Refusal("PATH_ESCAPE", f"manifest path escapes the pack root: {rel!r}")
        member = mount_pack / rel
        if _path_is_symlink(member):
            raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", f"{member} is a symlink")
        if not member.is_file():
            raise Refusal("MANIFEST_MEMBER_MISSING", f"manifest lists {rel} but it is absent")
        data = member.read_bytes()
        actual = _sha256(_canonical_bytes(data))
        if actual != digest:
            raise Refusal("MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH",
                          f"{rel}: copied digest {digest} != computed {actual}")
        listed_paths.add(rel)
        listed.append((rel, digest, data))

    on_disk: set[str] = set()
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(mount_pack, followlinks=False):
        dirnames.sort()
        filenames.sort()
        for d in dirnames:
            if _path_is_symlink(Path(dirpath) / d):
                raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", str(Path(dirpath) / d))
        for f in filenames:
            p = Path(dirpath) / f
            if _path_is_symlink(p):
                raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", str(p))
            rel = p.relative_to(mount_pack).as_posix()
            if rel == MANIFEST_NAME:
                continue
            on_disk.add(rel)
    extra = sorted(on_disk - listed_paths)
    if extra:
        raise Refusal("UNEXPECTED_EXTRA_FILE", f"pack carries unlisted file(s): {extra}")

    for rel, _digest, data in listed:
        if rel.endswith(".md") and release_commit not in data.decode("utf-8", "replace"):
            raise Refusal("RELEASE_STAMP_MISSING",
                          f"{rel} does not stamp the release commit {release_commit}")
    return listed


def compose_document(release_id: str, release_commit: str,
                     members: list[tuple[str, str, bytes]], size_cap: int) -> bytes:
    """Compose the single bounded markdown document (no truncation anywhere)."""
    lines: list[str] = [
        f"<!-- {FALLBACK_SCHEMA} DOC_MOUNT_ONLY -->",
        "# PIPD-LS-SP S4 Web fallback — single-document mount (DOC_MOUNT_ONLY)",
        "",
        f"- release_id: {release_id}",
        f"- release_commit: {release_commit}",
        "- doc_mount_only: true",
        f"- member_count: {len(members)}",
        f"- size_cap_bytes: {size_cap}",
        "",
        "> DOC_MOUNT_ONLY: this is a document drop, not an installed plugin, not a host-registered",
        "> skill and not a public directory listing (none exists yet). It executes nothing. Verify a",
        "> member against the inventory below before you rely on it.",
        "",
        "## Member inventory",
        "",
        "| member | sha256 |",
        "| --- | --- |",
    ]
    for rel, digest, _data in members:
        lines.append(f"| {rel} | {digest} |")
    for rel, _digest, data in members:
        lines += ["", f"## Member: {rel}", "", f"<!-- BEGIN MEMBER {rel} -->"]
        lines.append(data.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        lines.append(f"<!-- END MEMBER {rel} -->")
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    if not text.endswith("\n"):
        text += "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def write_exclusive(out_path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:
    out_path = Path(out_path)
    if _path_is_symlink(out_path):
        raise Refusal("DESTINATION_SYMLINK", f"destination {out_path} is a symlink")
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL
    try:
        fd = os.open(out_path, flags, 0o644)
    except FileExistsError as exc:
        raise Refusal("DESTINATION_EXISTS",
                      f"destination {out_path} already exists; refusing to overwrite") from exc
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(data)
    except BaseException:
        if out_path.exists() and not _path_is_symlink(out_path):
            out_path.unlink()
        raise


def build_fallback(*, mount_pack: Path, release_id: str, release_commit: str, out_path: Path,
                   size_cap: int = DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP) -> dict:
    if not HEX40.match(str(release_commit)):
        raise Refusal("RELEASE_COMMIT_INVALID",
                      f"release commit is not 40 hex chars: {release_commit!r}")
    if size_cap <= 0:
        raise Refusal("SIZE_CAP_INVALID", f"size cap must be positive: {size_cap!r}")
    members = load_and_verify_pack(mount_pack, release_commit)
    document = compose_document(release_id, release_commit, members, size_cap)
    if len(document) > size_cap:
        raise Refusal("SIZE_CAP_EXCEEDED",
                      f"composed document is {len(document)} bytes > cap {size_cap}; "
                      "refusing to truncate")
    write_exclusive(Path(out_path), document)
    return {
        "verdict": "BUILT",
        "out": str(out_path),
        "bytes": len(document),
        "sha256": _sha256(document),
        "member_count": len(members),
        "doc_mount_only": True,
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--mount-pack", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--release-id", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--release-commit", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--size-cap", type=int, default=DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        report = build_fallback(
            mount_pack=Path(args.mount_pack),
            release_id=args.release_id,
            release_commit=args.release_commit,
            out_path=Path(args.out),
            size_cap=args.size_cap,
        )
    except Refusal as exc:
        print(str(exc))
        return 2
    print(f"BUILT {report['out']} bytes={report['bytes']} sha256={report['sha256']} "
          f"members={report['member_count']} DOC_MOUNT_ONLY")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""WO-S4-WEB-02: build and verify the one versioned Web/ChatGPT mount pack.

This tool is the *only* writer for ``dist/mount/**``. It does three determinism-critical things,
and nothing else:

1. It derives ``MANIFEST.sha256`` **from the actual pack files** (relative POSIX paths, sorted,
   ``"<sha256>  <relpath>"`` one per line) and rewrites it into the pack root.
2. It builds the ZIP byte-identically on every run with the same inputs: entries rooted at the pack
   directory name, fixed ``ZipInfo.date_time`` (the 1980 ZIP epoch), fixed permission bits, fixed
   compression. ``MANIFEST.sha256`` is written **last** (the first manifest entry is therefore the
   last archive entry).
3. ``--verify`` recomputes the digest of every manifest-listed member from the ZIP bytes themselves
   and refuses, by name, any mutation, missing member, unmanifested member, or path that escapes the
   pack root. It never writes.

The tool declares no runtime authority: it is a stdlib-only build/verify utility, candidate-only.

CLI
---
``--pack-root DIR --out-zip FILE``   rebuild MANIFEST.sha256, then the ZIP (+ ``.sha256`` sidecar).
``--verify FILE``                    recompute and compare; exit 0 on PASS, non-zero on any refusal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

MANIFEST_NAME = "MANIFEST.sha256"
# The ZIP epoch. A constant date_time makes the archive reproducible across runs (zips otherwise
# embed the wall-clock mtime of each member).
FIXED_DATE_TIME = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
COMPRESS_LEVEL = 9


def _sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _member_bytes(path: Path) -> bytes:
    """The CANONICAL bytes of a pack member (EOL-normalised for text).

    S4EXT-R1 (F-S4EXT-008, found while repairing F001): the ZIP published as
    ``v0.1.1-preview.3`` captured CRLF member bytes -- it was built from a CRLF checkout, before
    ``.gitattributes`` pinned ``* text=auto eol=lf`` -- so its 8 members (and the manifest it
    embeds) do not match the same members in the LF-normalised tree, and the published bytes were
    NOT reproducible from the repository. Canonicalising text members to LF here means the
    manifest and the archive members are derived from ONE byte sequence, so a rebuild of the same
    source is byte-identical on any platform. Binary members (NUL byte / non-UTF-8) are never
    rewritten. ``verify_pack`` is deliberately NOT changed: it must keep re-deriving a member's
    digest from the bytes actually inside the ZIP.
    """
    data = path.read_bytes()
    if b"\x00" in data:
        return data
    try:
        data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return data
    return data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n").replace(b"\r", b"\n")


def _content_files(pack_root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """Every real file under the pack root except the manifest itself, sorted by rela. POSIX path."""
    files = [
        p for p in pack_root.rglob("*")
        if p.is_file() and p.name != MANIFEST_NAME
    ]
    return sorted(files, key=lambda p: p.relative_to(pack_root).as_posix())


def _manifest_text(pack_root: Path, files: list[Path]) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"{_sha256_bytes(_member_bytes(f))}  {f.relative_to(pack_root).as_posix()}"
        for f in files
    ]
    return ("\n".join(lines) + "\n") if lines else ""


def _write_member(zf: zipfile.ZipFile, arcname: str, data: bytes) -> None:
    info = zipfile.ZipInfo(arcname, date_time=FIXED_DATE_TIME)
    info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
    info.external_attr = 0o644 << 16  # fixed permission bits, no host-specific metadata
    info.create_system = 0            # fixed "creator" so the header bytes are stable
    zf.writestr(info, data, compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=COMPRESS_LEVEL)


def build_pack(pack_root: Path, out_zip: Path) -> dict:
    """Rebuild MANIFEST.sha256 from the pack files, then the ZIP. Returns a small report."""
    pack_root = Path(pack_root).resolve()
    out_zip = Path(out_zip).resolve()
    if not pack_root.is_dir():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"pack root is not a directory: {pack_root}")

    files = _content_files(pack_root)
    manifest_text = _manifest_text(pack_root, files)
    manifest_bytes = manifest_text.encode("utf-8")
    (pack_root / MANIFEST_NAME).write_bytes(manifest_bytes)

    root_name = pack_root.name
    out_zip.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(out_zip, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=COMPRESS_LEVEL) as zf:
        for f in files:
            rel = f.relative_to(pack_root).as_posix()
            _write_member(zf, f"{root_name}/{rel}", _member_bytes(f))
        # MANIFEST.sha256 is the LAST archive entry (its first content line is written last).
        _write_member(zf, f"{root_name}/{MANIFEST_NAME}", manifest_bytes)

    digest = _sha256_bytes(out_zip.read_bytes())
    sidecar = out_zip.with_name(out_zip.name + ".sha256")
    sidecar.write_bytes(f"{digest}  {out_zip.name}\n".encode("utf-8"))
    return {
        "pack_root": str(pack_root),
        "out_zip": str(out_zip),
        "members": len(files) + 1,  # content files + the manifest
        "zip_sha256": digest,
        "sidecar": str(sidecar),
    }


def _parse_manifest(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Parse ``"<sha256>  <relpath>"`` lines. Returns [(digest, relpath), ...]."""
    entries: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if "  " not in line:
            raise ValueError(f"malformed manifest line (no two-space separator): {line!r}")
        digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
        entries.append((digest.strip(), rel.strip()))
    return entries


def verify_pack(zip_path: Path) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    """Recompute the manifest from the ZIP bytes. Returns (ok, problems)."""
    zip_path = Path(zip_path).resolve()
    problems: list[str] = []
    if not zip_path.is_file():
        return False, [f"ZIP_NOT_FOUND: {zip_path}"]

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as zf:
        names = zf.namelist()

        # 1. No member may escape the pack root (no absolute path, no '..', no backslash).
        for name in names:
            parts = name.split("/")
            if (name.startswith("/") or ".." in parts or "\\" in name
                    or parts[0] in ("", ".")):
                problems.append(f"ESCAPES_PACK_ROOT: {name}")

        if not names:
            return False, ["EMPTY_ZIP"]
        root_name = names[0].split("/")[0]
        manifest_arcname = f"{root_name}/{MANIFEST_NAME}"
        if manifest_arcname not in names:
            return False, [f"MANIFEST_MISSING: {MANIFEST_NAME}"]

        # 2. Every member must live under the single pack-root segment.
        for name in names:
            if not name.startswith(root_name + "/"):
                problems.append(f"OUTSIDE_PACK_ROOT: {name}")

        entries = _parse_manifest(zf.read(manifest_arcname).decode("utf-8"))
        if not entries:
            problems.append("MANIFEST_EMPTY")

        manifest_paths = set()
        for digest, rel in entries:
            manifest_paths.add(rel)
            arcname = f"{root_name}/{rel}"
            if arcname not in names:
                problems.append(f"MANIFEST_ENTRY_NOT_IN_ZIP: {rel}")
                continue
            actual = _sha256_bytes(zf.read(arcname))
            if actual != digest:
                problems.append(f"MUTATED_MEMBER: {rel}")

        # 3. Every content member (i.e. everything but the manifest) must be listed.
        for name in names:
            if name == manifest_arcname:
                continue
            rel = name[len(root_name) + 1:]
            if rel not in manifest_paths:
                problems.append(f"UNMANIFESTED_FILE: {rel}")

    return (not problems), problems


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--pack-root", help="pack authoring directory (its name roots the ZIP)")
    ap.add_argument("--out-zip", help="destination ZIP path when building")
    ap.add_argument("--verify", help="verify an existing ZIP; exit 0 on PASS, non-zero on refusal")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.verify:
        ok, problems = verify_pack(Path(args.verify))
        if ok:
            print(f"VERIFY PASS: {args.verify}")
            return 0
        print(f"VERIFY FAIL: {args.verify}")
        for p in problems:
            print(f"  - {p}")
        return 1

    if not args.pack_root or not args.out_zip:
        ap.error("either --verify FILE, or both --pack-root DIR and --out-zip FILE, are required")
    report = build_pack(Path(args.pack_root), Path(args.out_zip))
    print(
        "BUILD OK: "
        f"pack_root={report['pack_root']} "
        f"out_zip={report['out_zip']} "
        f"members={report['members']} "
        f"zip_sha256={report['zip_sha256']}"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

class WebProjectionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.td = Path(self._td.name)
        self.out = self.td / "web"
        P.project_surfaces(ROOT, self.out)

    def tearDown(self):
        self._td.cleanup()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- positive

    def test_exact_semantic_documents_not_site_ui(self):
        present = {p.name for p in self.out.glob("PIPD_*.md")}
        self.assertEqual(present, DOCS)
        result = P.check_web_surface(ROOT, self.out)
        self.assertEqual(result["verdict"], "PASS", result["first_failing_invariant"])
        self.assertEqual(result["denominator"]["ratio"], "5/5")

    def test_docs_carry_source_objects_schema_version_hash_loss_nack(self):
        for name in sorted(DOCS):
            text = (self.out / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            match = META_RE.search(text)
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"{name} has no PIPD-DOC-META block")
            meta = json.loads(match.group(1))
            self.assertEqual(meta["schema"], P.SCHEMA_DOC_META)
            self.assertEqual(meta["schema_version"], P.SCHEMA_VERSION)
            self.assertTrue(meta["source_objects"], f"{name} declares no source objects")
            for ref in meta["source_objects"]:
                for key in ("object_id", "schema", "schema_version", "source_path", "source_hash"):
                    self.assertTrue(ref.get(key), f"{name} source ref missing {key}")
            self.assertTrue(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", meta["source_hash"]),
                            f"{name} source hash is not a sha256")
            self.assertTrue(meta["capability_loss"], f"{name} has no CapabilityLoss record")
            self.assertTrue(meta["nack"], f"{name} has no NACK record")
            self.assertEqual(meta["capability_loss"][0]["record_type"], "CapabilityLoss")
            self.assertEqual(meta["nack"][0]["record_type"], "NACK")
            self.assertTrue(meta["denominator"])

    def test_content_derived_from_canonical_objects_not_free_text(self):
        """Cross-check derivation with independent parsing, not via the projector."""
        registry = json.loads((ROOT / "schemas" / "registry.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        core = (self.out / "PIPD_CANONICAL_CORE.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        schemas_doc = (self.out / "PIPD_ARTIFACT_SCHEMAS.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for fam in registry["families"]:
            self.assertIn(fam["contract"], core, "canonical core misses a contract family")
            self.assertIn(fam["contract"], schemas_doc)
            schema = json.loads(
                (ROOT / fam["schema_file"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertIn(schema["$id"], schemas_doc, "schema doc misses a $id")
            for field in schema.get("required", []):
                self.assertIn(field, schemas_doc)
        prof_text = (ROOT / "src" / "pipd_ls_sp" / "profiles.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for name in re.findall(r'"(LITE|STANDARD|ASSURED)"', prof_text):
            self.assertIn(name, (self.out / "PIPD_ROUTER_PROFILES.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        handoff = (self.out / "PIPD_EVAL_HANDOFF.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for stage in ("S5", "S6", "S7", "S8"):
            self.assertIn(stage, handoff)
        bootstrap = (self.out / "PIPD_BOOTSTRAP.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("schemas/registry.json", bootstrap)

    def test_optional_site_ui_excluded_from_web_denominator(self):

Cases:
1. exact projection: a frozen mount pack (a small `MANIFEST.sha256` plus its member documents) is
   reproduced into ONE markdown document whose embedded section carries the source bytes verbatim,
   plus the member inventory table and the `DOC_MOUNT_ONLY` ceiling stamp.
2. stale release stamp: a document that names the release but not the pinned commit (or vice versa)
   is REFUSED.
3. over-cap input is REFUSED with no truncation - and assert the destination file does **not** exist
   afterwards (not merely that an exception was raised).
4. a source member whose digest disagrees with the manifest is REFUSED.
5. an unexpected extra file in the mount (absent from the manifest) is REFUSED, and so is a manifest
   entry with no file.
6. an existing destination file is REFUSED (`O_EXCL` semantics) and its bytes are unchanged.
7. a symlinked destination is REFUSED **and the sentinel file behind the symlink is byte-identical
   afterwards**.
8. a manifest that is itself a symlink, or a member that escapes the mount root, is REFUSED.
9. a non-UTF-8 / non-text member type is REFUSED.
10. the refusal path is a **non-zero exit** through the module's CLI `main()` equivalent, and the
    output above the cap is refused rather than trimmed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""S4POST Stage B: project one frozen Web mount pack into ONE bounded fallback document.

There is no public directory listing for the plugin yet, so the current Web route is a single
markdown document a reader can attach to a conversation or a Knowledge base. This tool builds that
document from a *frozen mount pack* (a directory carrying ``MANIFEST.sha256``) and is fail-closed:
it REFUSES (typed reason, non-zero exit) rather than warn on

  * ``MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH``  a member's bytes no longer match ``MANIFEST.sha256``
  * ``MEMBER_SYMLINK``            a symlinked member (or pack) is present
  * ``PATH_ESCAPE``               a manifest path escapes the pack root
  * ``UNEXPECTED_EXTRA_FILE``     a file exists in the pack that the manifest does not list
  * ``RELEASE_STAMP_MISSING``     a member document does not stamp the release commit
  * ``SIZE_CAP_EXCEEDED``         the composed document would exceed the cap (NEVER truncated)
  * ``DESTINATION_EXISTS`` / ``DESTINATION_SYMLINK``  the output file already exists

The document is written with ``O_EXCL`` and stamps ``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY`` plus the member inventory. No
timestamp is embedded, so two builds are byte-identical.

CLI
---
``--mount-pack DIR``      unpacked frozen mount pack (contains MANIFEST.sha256)
``--release-id TEXT``     e.g. v0.1.1-preview.3 (informational stamp)
``--release-commit HEX40`` the commit the members must stamp
``--size-cap BYTES``      hard cap for the composed document (default 524288)
``--out FILE``            destination markdown file (must not exist)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MANIFEST_NAME = "MANIFEST.sha256"
FALLBACK_SCHEMA = "PIPD-WEB-FALLBACK/1"
DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP = 524288
HEX40 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")


class Refusal(Exception):
    """A fail-closed refusal. ``code`` is the machine-checkable typed reason."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"REFUSED {code}: {detail}")
        self.code = code
        self.detail = detail


def _path_is_symlink(path) -> bool:
    """Seam for tests: a single predicate the destination gate consults."""
    return os.path.islink(path)


def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _canonical_bytes(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if b"\x00" in data:
        return data
    try:
        data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return data
    return data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n").replace(b"\r", b"\n")


def _parse_manifest(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    entries: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if "  " not in line:
            raise Refusal("MANIFEST_INVALID", f"line has no two-space separator: {line!r}")
        digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
        digest, rel = digest.strip(), rel.strip()
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", digest):
            raise Refusal("MANIFEST_INVALID", f"digest is not 64 hex chars: {digest!r}")
        entries.append((digest, rel))
    if not entries:
        raise Refusal("MANIFEST_INVALID", "MANIFEST.sha256 lists no members")
    return entries


def _escapes(rel: str) -> bool:
    parts = rel.replace("\\", "/").split("/")
    return (rel.startswith("/") or "\\" in rel or ":" in rel or ".." in parts
            or any(part == "" for part in parts) or parts[0] in (".", ""))


def load_and_verify_pack(mount_pack: Path, release_commit: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, bytes]]:
    """Return [(rel, sha256, bytes), ...] for a verified, exactly-listed pack."""
    mount_pack = Path(mount_pack)
    if _path_is_symlink(mount_pack):
        raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", f"mount pack {mount_pack} is a symlink")
    if not mount_pack.is_dir():
        raise Refusal("MOUNT_PACK_MISSING", f"mount pack is not a directory: {mount_pack}")
    manifest_path = mount_pack / MANIFEST_NAME
    if _path_is_symlink(manifest_path):
        raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", f"{manifest_path} is a symlink")
    if not manifest_path.is_file():
        raise Refusal("MANIFEST_MISSING", f"{manifest_path} is absent")
    entries = _parse_manifest(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    listed: list[tuple[str, str, bytes]] = []
    listed_paths: set[str] = set()
    for digest, rel in entries:
        if _escapes(rel):
            raise Refusal("PATH_ESCAPE", f"manifest path escapes the pack root: {rel!r}")
        member = mount_pack / rel
        if _path_is_symlink(member):
            raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", f"{member} is a symlink")
        if not member.is_file():
            raise Refusal("MANIFEST_MEMBER_MISSING", f"manifest lists {rel} but it is absent")
        data = member.read_bytes()
        actual = _sha256(_canonical_bytes(data))
        if actual != digest:
            raise Refusal("MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH",
                          f"{rel}: copied digest {digest} != computed {actual}")
        listed_paths.add(rel)
        listed.append((rel, digest, data))

    on_disk: set[str] = set()
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(mount_pack, followlinks=False):
        dirnames.sort()
        filenames.sort()
        for d in dirnames:
            if _path_is_symlink(Path(dirpath) / d):
                raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", str(Path(dirpath) / d))
        for f in filenames:
            p = Path(dirpath) / f
            if _path_is_symlink(p):
                raise Refusal("MEMBER_SYMLINK", str(p))
            rel = p.relative_to(mount_pack).as_posix()
            if rel == MANIFEST_NAME:
                continue
            on_disk.add(rel)
    extra = sorted(on_disk - listed_paths)
    if extra:
        raise Refusal("UNEXPECTED_EXTRA_FILE", f"pack carries unlisted file(s): {extra}")

    for rel, _digest, data in listed:
        if rel.endswith(".md") and release_commit not in data.decode("utf-8", "replace"):
            raise Refusal("RELEASE_STAMP_MISSING",
                          f"{rel} does not stamp the release commit {release_commit}")
    return listed


def compose_document(release_id: str, release_commit: str,
                     members: list[tuple[str, str, bytes]], size_cap: int) -> bytes:
    """Compose the single bounded markdown document (no truncation anywhere)."""
    lines: list[str] = [
        f"<!-- {FALLBACK_SCHEMA} DOC_MOUNT_ONLY -->",
        "# PIPD-LS-SP S4 Web fallback — single-document mount (DOC_MOUNT_ONLY)",
        "",
        f"- release_id: {release_id}",
        f"- release_commit: {release_commit}",
        "- doc_mount_only: true",
        f"- member_count: {len(members)}",
        f"- size_cap_bytes: {size_cap}",
        "",
        "> DOC_MOUNT_ONLY: this is a document drop, not an installed plugin, not a host-registered",
        "> skill and not a public directory listing (none exists yet). It executes nothing. Verify a",
        "> member against the inventory below before you rely on it.",
        "",
        "## Member inventory",
        "",
        "| member | sha256 |",
        "| --- | --- |",
    ]
    for rel, digest, _data in members:
        lines.append(f"| {rel} | {digest} |")
    for rel, _digest, data in members:
        lines += ["", f"## Member: {rel}", "", f"<!-- BEGIN MEMBER {rel} -->"]
        lines.append(data.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        lines.append(f"<!-- END MEMBER {rel} -->")
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    if not text.endswith("\n"):
        text += "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def write_exclusive(out_path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:
    out_path = Path(out_path)
    if _path_is_symlink(out_path):
        raise Refusal("DESTINATION_SYMLINK", f"destination {out_path} is a symlink")
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL
    try:
        fd = os.open(out_path, flags, 0o644)
    except FileExistsError as exc:
        raise Refusal("DESTINATION_EXISTS",
                      f"destination {out_path} already exists; refusing to overwrite") from exc
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(data)
    except BaseException:
        if out_path.exists() and not _path_is_symlink(out_path):
            out_path.unlink()
        raise


def build_fallback(*, mount_pack: Path, release_id: str, release_commit: str, out_path: Path,
                   size_cap: int = DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP) -> dict:
    if not HEX40.match(str(release_commit)):
        raise Refusal("RELEASE_COMMIT_INVALID",
                      f"release commit is not 40 hex chars: {release_commit!r}")
    if size_cap <= 0:
        raise Refusal("SIZE_CAP_INVALID", f"size cap must be positive: {size_cap!r}")
    members = load_and_verify_pack(mount_pack, release_commit)
    document = compose_document(release_id, release_commit, members, size_cap)
    if len(document) > size_cap:
        raise Refusal("SIZE_CAP_EXCEEDED",
                      f"composed document is {len(document)} bytes > cap {size_cap}; "
                      "refusing to truncate")
    write_exclusive(Path(out_path), document)
    return {
        "verdict": "BUILT",
        "out": str(out_path),
        "bytes": len(document),
        "sha256": _sha256(document),
        "member_count": len(members),
        "doc_mount_only": True,
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--mount-pack", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--release-id", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--release-commit", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--size-cap", type=int, default=DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        report = build_fallback(
            mount_pack=Path(args.mount_pack),
            release_id=args.release_id,
            release_commit=args.release_commit,
            out_path=Path(args.out),
            size_cap=args.size_cap,
        )
    except Refusal as exc:
        print(str(exc))
        return 2
    print(f"BUILT {report['out']} bytes={report['bytes']} sha256={report['sha256']} "
          f"members={report['member_count']} DOC_MOUNT_ONLY")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

objects/profiles, each carrying source objects (id/schema/version), a source
hash, a CapabilityLoss record and a NACK record. OPTIONAL_SITE_UI is excluded

Refusal mutations: MUT-WEB-WRONGSET (including the audit's falsification — the

from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

from pipd_ls_sp import projection as P
