        "PIPD_ARTIFACT_SCHEMAS.md", "PIPD_EVAL_HANDOFF.md"}
META_RE = re.compile(r"<!--PIPD-DOC-META\s*\n(.*?)\n-->", re.S)


def make_source_root(td: Path) -> Path:
    """A minimal source root: the canonical objects the projector reads."""
    troot = td / "repo"
    (troot / "src" / "pipd_ls_sp").mkdir(parents=True)
    (troot / "fixtures" / "s5_s8").mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copytree(ROOT / "schemas", troot / "schemas")
    shutil.copy(ROOT / "src" / "pipd_ls_sp" / "profiles.py",
                troot / "src" / "pipd_ls_sp" / "profiles.py")
    for f in (ROOT / "fixtures" / "s5_s8").iterdir():
        shutil.copy(f, troot / "fixtures" / "s5_s8" / f.name)
    return troot


class WebProjectionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.td = Path(self._td.name)
        self.out = self.td / "web"
        P.project_surfaces(ROOT, self.out)

    def tearDown(self):
        self._td.cleanup()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- positive

    def test_exact_semantic_documents_not_site_ui(self):
        present = {p.name for p in self.out.glob("PIPD_*.md")}
        self.assertEqual(present, DOCS)
        result = P.check_web_surface(ROOT, self.out)
        self.assertEqual(result["verdict"], "PASS", result["first_failing_invariant"])
        self.assertEqual(result["denominator"]["ratio"], "5/5")

    def test_docs_carry_source_objects_schema_version_hash_loss_nack(self):
        for name in sorted(DOCS):
            text = (self.out / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            match = META_RE.search(text)
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"{name} has no PIPD-DOC-META block")
            meta = json.loads(match.group(1))
            self.assertEqual(meta["schema"], P.SCHEMA_DOC_META)
            self.assertEqual(meta["schema_version"], P.SCHEMA_VERSION)
            self.assertTrue(meta["source_objects"], f"{name} declares no source objects")
            for ref in meta["source_objects"]:
                for key in ("object_id", "schema", "schema_version", "source_path", "source_hash"):
                    self.assertTrue(ref.get(key), f"{name} source ref missing {key}")
            self.assertTrue(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", meta["source_hash"]),
                            f"{name} source hash is not a sha256")
            self.assertTrue(meta["capability_loss"], f"{name} has no CapabilityLoss record")
            self.assertTrue(meta["nack"], f"{name} has no NACK record")
            self.assertEqual(meta["capability_loss"][0]["record_type"], "CapabilityLoss")
            self.assertEqual(meta["nack"][0]["record_type"], "NACK")
            self.assertTrue(meta["denominator"])

    def test_content_derived_from_canonical_objects_not_free_text(self):

        registry = json.loads((ROOT / "schemas" / "registry.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

        handoff = (self.out / "PIPD_EVAL_HANDOFF.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        bootstrap = (self.out / "PIPD_BOOTSTRAP.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("schemas/registry.json", bootstrap)

    def test_optional_site_ui_excluded_from_web_denominator(self):

    def test_stale_source_is_regenerated(self):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""WO-S4-WEB-02: build and verify the one versioned Web/ChatGPT mount pack.

This tool is the *only* writer for ``dist/mount/**``. It does three determinism-critical things,
and nothing else:

1. It derives ``MANIFEST.sha256`` **from the actual pack files** (relative POSIX paths, sorted,
   ``"<sha256>  <relpath>"`` one per line) and rewrites it into the pack root.
2. It builds the ZIP byte-identically on every run with the same inputs: entries rooted at the pack
   directory name, fixed ``ZipInfo.date_time`` (the 1980 ZIP epoch), fixed permission bits, fixed
   compression. ``MANIFEST.sha256`` is written **last** (the first manifest entry is therefore the
   last archive entry).
3. ``--verify`` recomputes the digest of every manifest-listed member from the ZIP bytes themselves
   and refuses, by name, any mutation, missing member, unmanifested member, or path that escapes the
   pack root. It never writes.

The tool declares no runtime authority: it is a stdlib-only build/verify utility, candidate-only.

CLI
---
``--pack-root DIR --out-zip FILE``   rebuild MANIFEST.sha256, then the ZIP (+ ``.sha256`` sidecar).
``--verify FILE``                    recompute and compare; exit 0 on PASS, non-zero on any refusal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

MANIFEST_NAME = "MANIFEST.sha256"
# The ZIP epoch. A constant date_time makes the archive reproducible across runs (zips otherwise
# embed the wall-clock mtime of each member).
FIXED_DATE_TIME = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
COMPRESS_LEVEL = 9


def _sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _member_bytes(path: Path) -> bytes:
    """The CANONICAL bytes of a pack member (EOL-normalised for text).

    S4EXT-R1 (F-S4EXT-008, found while repairing F001): the ZIP published as
    ``v0.1.1-preview.3`` captured CRLF member bytes -- it was built from a CRLF checkout, before
    ``.gitattributes`` pinned ``* text=auto eol=lf`` -- so its 8 members (and the manifest it
    embeds) do not match the same members in the LF-normalised tree, and the published bytes were
    NOT reproducible from the repository. Canonicalising text members to LF here means the
    manifest and the archive members are derived from ONE byte sequence, so a rebuild of the same
    source is byte-identical on any platform. Binary members (NUL byte / non-UTF-8) are never
    rewritten. ``verify_pack`` is deliberately NOT changed: it must keep re-deriving a member's
    digest from the bytes actually inside the ZIP.
    """
    data = path.read_bytes()
    if b"\x00" in data:
        return data
    try:
        data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return data
    return data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n").replace(b"\r", b"\n")


def _content_files(pack_root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """Every real file under the pack root except the manifest itself, sorted by rela. POSIX path."""
    files = [
        p for p in pack_root.rglob("*")
        if p.is_file() and p.name != MANIFEST_NAME
    ]
    return sorted(files, key=lambda p: p.relative_to(pack_root).as_posix())


def _manifest_text(pack_root: Path, files: list[Path]) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"{_sha256_bytes(_member_bytes(f))}  {f.relative_to(pack_root).as_posix()}"
        for f in files
    ]
    return ("\n".join(lines) + "\n") if lines else ""


def _write_member(zf: zipfile.ZipFile, arcname: str, data: bytes) -> None:
    info = zipfile.ZipInfo(arcname, date_time=FIXED_DATE_TIME)
    info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
    info.external_attr = 0o644 << 16  # fixed permission bits, no host-specific metadata
    info.create_system = 0            # fixed "creator" so the header bytes are stable
    zf.writestr(info, data, compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=COMPRESS_LEVEL)


def build_pack(pack_root: Path, out_zip: Path) -> dict:
    """Rebuild MANIFEST.sha256 from the pack files, then the ZIP. Returns a small report."""
    pack_root = Path(pack_root).resolve()
    out_zip = Path(out_zip).resolve()
    if not pack_root.is_dir():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"pack root is not a directory: {pack_root}")

    files = _content_files(pack_root)
    manifest_text = _manifest_text(pack_root, files)
    manifest_bytes = manifest_text.encode("utf-8")
    (pack_root / MANIFEST_NAME).write_bytes(manifest_bytes)

    root_name = pack_root.name
    out_zip.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(out_zip, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=COMPRESS_LEVEL) as zf:
        for f in files:
            rel = f.relative_to(pack_root).as_posix()
            _write_member(zf, f"{root_name}/{rel}", _member_bytes(f))
        # MANIFEST.sha256 is the LAST archive entry (its first content line is written last).
        _write_member(zf, f"{root_name}/{MANIFEST_NAME}", manifest_bytes)

    digest = _sha256_bytes(out_zip.read_bytes())
    sidecar = out_zip.with_name(out_zip.name + ".sha256")
    sidecar.write_bytes(f"{digest}  {out_zip.name}\n".encode("utf-8"))
    return {
        "pack_root": str(pack_root),
        "out_zip": str(out_zip),
        "members": len(files) + 1,  # content files + the manifest
        "zip_sha256": digest,
        "sidecar": str(sidecar),
    }


def _parse_manifest(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Parse ``"<sha256>  <relpath>"`` lines. Returns [(digest, relpath), ...]."""
    entries: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if "  " not in line:
            raise ValueError(f"malformed manifest line (no two-space separator): {line!r}")
        digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
        entries.append((digest.strip(), rel.strip()))
    return entries


def verify_pack(zip_path: Path) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    """Recompute the manifest from the ZIP bytes. Returns (ok, problems)."""
    zip_path = Path(zip_path).resolve()
    problems: list[str] = []
    if not zip_path.is_file():
        return False, [f"ZIP_NOT_FOUND: {zip_path}"]

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as zf:
        names = zf.namelist()

        # 1. No member may escape the pack root (no absolute path, no '..', no backslash).
        for name in names:
            parts = name.split("/")
            if (name.startswith("/") or ".." in parts or "\\" in name
                    or parts[0] in ("", ".")):
                problems.append(f"ESCAPES_PACK_ROOT: {name}")

        if not names:
            return False, ["EMPTY_ZIP"]
        root_name = names[0].split("/")[0]
        manifest_arcname = f"{root_name}/{MANIFEST_NAME}"
        if manifest_arcname not in names:
            return False, [f"MANIFEST_MISSING: {MANIFEST_NAME}"]

        # 2. Every member must live under the single pack-root segment.
        for name in names:
            if not name.startswith(root_name + "/"):
                problems.append(f"OUTSIDE_PACK_ROOT: {name}")

        entries = _parse_manifest(zf.read(manifest_arcname).decode("utf-8"))
        if not entries:
            problems.append("MANIFEST_EMPTY")

        manifest_paths = set()
        for digest, rel in entries:
            manifest_paths.add(rel)
            arcname = f"{root_name}/{rel}"
            if arcname not in names:
                problems.append(f"MANIFEST_ENTRY_NOT_IN_ZIP: {rel}")
                continue
            actual = _sha256_bytes(zf.read(arcname))
            if actual != digest:
                problems.append(f"MUTATED_MEMBER: {rel}")

        # 3. Every content member (i.e. everything but the manifest) must be listed.
        for name in names:
            if name == manifest_arcname:
                continue
            rel = name[len(root_name) + 1:]
            if rel not in manifest_paths:
                problems.append(f"UNMANIFESTED_FILE: {rel}")

    return (not problems), problems


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--pack-root", help="pack authoring directory (its name roots the ZIP)")
    ap.add_argument("--out-zip", help="destination ZIP path when building")
    ap.add_argument("--verify", help="verify an existing ZIP; exit 0 on PASS, non-zero on refusal")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.verify:
        ok, problems = verify_pack(Path(args.verify))
        if ok:
            print(f"VERIFY PASS: {args.verify}")
            return 0
        print(f"VERIFY FAIL: {args.verify}")
        for p in problems:
            print(f"  - {p}")
        return 1

    if not args.pack_root or not args.out_zip:
        ap.error("either --verify FILE, or both --pack-root DIR and --out-zip FILE, are required")
    report = build_pack(Path(args.pack_root), Path(args.out_zip))
    print(
        "BUILD OK: "
        f"pack_root={report['pack_root']} "
        f"out_zip={report['out_zip']} "
        f"members={report['members']} "
        f"zip_sha256={report['zip_sha256']}"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _read_zip(path: Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zf:
        return {n: zf.read(n) for n in zf.namelist()}


def _write_zip(path: Path, members: dict[str, bytes]) -> None:
    """Rewrite a zip deterministically, preserving the tool's fixed per-member stamp."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for name, data in members.items():
            info = zipfile.ZipInfo(name, date_time=BMP.FIXED_DATE_TIME)
            info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
            info.external_attr = 0o644 << 16
            info.create_system = 0
            zf.writestr(info, data)


class MountPackBuildTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.td = Path(self._td.name)

    def tearDown(self):
        self._td.cleanup()

    def _build(self, name="pack") -> Path:
        pack = self.td / PACK_NAME
        if not pack.exists():
            shutil.copytree(PACK_ROOT, pack)
        out = self.td / f"{name}.zip"
        BMP.build_pack(pack, out)
        return out

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- positive

    def test_pack_directory_has_exact_expected_files(self):
        present = {p.relative_to(PACK_ROOT).as_posix() for p in PACK_ROOT.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
        self.assertEqual(present, set(CONTENT_FILES) | {BMP.MANIFEST_NAME})

    def test_build_is_byte_deterministic(self):
        a = self._build("a")
        b = self._build("b")
        self.assertEqual(a.read_bytes(), b.read_bytes(), "same inputs must yield identical ZIP bytes")

    def test_verify_passes_and_names_nothing(self):
        out = self._build()
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertTrue(ok, problems)
        self.assertEqual(problems, [])

    def test_manifest_recomputes_from_members(self):
        out = self._build()
        members = _read_zip(out)
        manifest = members[f"{PACK_NAME}/{BMP.MANIFEST_NAME}"].decode("utf-8")
        entries = {
            rel: digest
            for digest, rel in (line.split("  ", 1) for line in manifest.splitlines() if line.strip())
        }
        self.assertEqual(set(entries), set(CONTENT_FILES))
        for rel in CONTENT_FILES:
            self.assertEqual(entries[rel], _sha256(members[f"{PACK_NAME}/{rel}"]))
        self.assertEqual(list(entries), sorted(entries))

    def test_manifest_is_last_archive_entry(self):
        out = self._build()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(out) as zf:
            names = zf.namelist()
        self.assertEqual(names[-1], f"{PACK_NAME}/{BMP.MANIFEST_NAME}")
        first_entry_rel = (_read_zip(out)[f"{PACK_NAME}/{BMP.MANIFEST_NAME}"]
                           .decode("utf-8").splitlines()[0].split("  ", 1)[1])
        self.assertNotEqual(first_entry_rel, BMP.MANIFEST_NAME)

    def test_all_members_are_stamped_fixed(self):
        out = self._build()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(out) as zf:
            for info in zf.infolist():
                self.assertEqual(info.date_time, BMP.FIXED_DATE_TIME)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ negatives

    def test_mutated_member_is_refused_and_named(self):
        out = self._build()
        members = _read_zip(out)
        target = f"{PACK_NAME}/references/PIPD_S4_CORE.md"
        members[target] = members[target] + b"\n<!-- tampered -->\n"
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("MUTATED_MEMBER: references/PIPD_S4_CORE.md", problems)

    def test_member_not_in_manifest_is_refused_and_named(self):
        out = self._build()
        members = _read_zip(out)
        members[f"{PACK_NAME}/EXTRA.md"] = b"leak\n"
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("UNMANIFESTED_FILE: EXTRA.md", problems)

    def test_manifest_entry_missing_from_zip_is_refused_and_named(self):
        out = self._build()
        members = _read_zip(out)
        del members[f"{PACK_NAME}/references/PIPD_EXAMPLES.md"]
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("MANIFEST_ENTRY_NOT_IN_ZIP: references/PIPD_EXAMPLES.md", problems)

    def test_path_escaping_pack_root_is_refused_and_named(self):
        out = self.td / "escape.zip"
        members = _read_zip(self._build())
        members["../evil.md"] = b"escape\n"
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("ESCAPES_PACK_ROOT: ../evil.md", problems)

    def test_absolute_path_is_refused(self):
        out = self.td / "abs.zip"
        members = _read_zip(self._build())
        members["/etc/evil.md"] = b"escape\n"
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("ESCAPES_PACK_ROOT: /etc/evil.md", problems)

    def test_verify_nonexistent_zip_refused(self):
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(self.td / "nope.zip")
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertTrue(any(p.startswith("ZIP_NOT_FOUND") for p in problems))

    # ------------------------------------------------ content requirements

    def test_every_document_carries_locator_and_release_identity(self):
        for rel in CONTENT_FILES:
            text = (PACK_ROOT / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIn(RELEASE_IDENTITY, text, f"{rel} lacks the release identity")
            self.assertIn(RELEASE_TAG_COMMIT, text, f"{rel} lacks the tag commit")
            self.assertIn("Source Locators", text, f"{rel} lacks a source locator section")

    def test_eight_existing_skills_and_no_ninth(self):
        index = (PACK_ROOT / "references/PIPD_8_SKILLS_INDEX.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for skill in ("pipd-route-intake", "pipd-authority-source", "pipd-profile-tailor",
                      "pipd-pi-compile", "pipd-pd-bind", "pipd-execution-contract",
                      "pipd-assurance-tqaep", "pipd-package-project"):
            self.assertIn(skill, index)
        dispatcher = (PACK_ROOT / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("dispatcher", dispatcher.lower())
        self.assertIn("not a ninth skill", dispatcher.lower())
        for skill in ("pipd-route-intake", "pipd-package-project"):
            self.assertIn(skill, dispatcher)

    def test_dispatcher_declares_triggers_and_non_triggers(self):
        text = (PACK_ROOT / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("## Trigger", text)
        self.assertIn("## Non-trigger", text)

                     "S5_S6_NOT_AUTHORISED", "UNKNOWN_RISK_NOT_ASSESSED"):
            self.assertIn(code, text)

    def test_readme_mount_marks_unavailable_capabilities(self):
        text = (PACK_ROOT / "README_MOUNT.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for capability in ("tool execution", "repository writing", "CLI invocation",
                           "HITL authority", "network / file access"):
            self.assertIn(capability, text, f"README_MOUNT misses capability row: {capability}")
        self.assertGreaterEqual(text.count("NOT_AVAILABLE"), 5)
        self.assertIn("Plugins", text)
        self.assertIn("Create -> Upload", text)
        self.assertIn("did not exercise", text.lower())
        self.assertIn("external executor", text.lower())

    def test_quickstart_prompt_bounds_the_role(self):
        text = (PACK_ROOT / "PIPD_LS_SP_QUICKSTART_PROMPT.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        low = text.lower()
        self.assertIn("design assistant", low)
        for doc in ("SKILL.md", "PIPD_S4_CORE.md", "PIPD_SOURCE_MAP.md"):
            self.assertIn(doc, text)
        self.assertIn("executor", low)
        self.assertIn("typed refusal", low)
        self.assertIn("never fabricate", low)
        for part in ("SOURCE LOCATORS", "ACTUAL EVIDENCE", "CLAIM CEILING", "NEXT STEP"):
            self.assertIn(part, text)

    def test_pack_contains_no_obvious_secret(self):
        banned = re.compile(r"(gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|"
                            r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----)")
        for rel in CONTENT_FILES:
            text = (PACK_ROOT / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIsNone(banned.search(text), f"{rel} appears to contain a secret")

    # --------------------------------------------------- published artifact

    def test_published_zip_verifies_and_matches_sidecar(self):
        self.assertTrue(ZIP.is_file(), "the published ZIP is missing; run the build command")
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(ZIP)
        self.assertTrue(ok, problems)
        digest = _sha256(ZIP.read_bytes())
        recorded = SIDECAR.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split()[0]
        self.assertEqual(digest, recorded)

    def test_uat_evidence_file_coverage(self):
        self.assertTrue(UAT.is_file(), "the UAT evidence file is missing")
        data = json.loads(UAT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        cases = {c["case_id"]: c for c in data["cases"]}
        self.assertEqual(len(cases), 5)
        for cid, case in cases.items():
            for key in ("fixed_input", "expected", "observed", "raw_output", "verdict",
                        "claim_ceiling"):
                self.assertIn(key, case, f"{cid} missing {key}")
            self.assertIn(case["verdict"], ("PASS", "FAIL", "NOT_SUPPORTED"))
        for cid, case in cases.items():
            if case["verdict"] != "PASS":
                self.assertEqual(case["verdict"], "NOT_SUPPORTED", cid)
                self.assertTrue(case.get("reason"), f"{cid} needs a reason")

Cases:
1. exact projection: a frozen mount pack (a small `MANIFEST.sha256` plus its member documents) is
   reproduced into ONE markdown document whose embedded section carries the source bytes verbatim,
   plus the member inventory table and the `DOC_MOUNT_ONLY` ceiling stamp.
2. stale release stamp: a document that names the release but not the pinned commit (or vice versa)
   is REFUSED.
3. over-cap input is REFUSED with no truncation - and assert the destination file does **not** exist
   afterwards (not merely that an exception was raised).
4. a source member whose digest disagrees with the manifest is REFUSED.
5. an unexpected extra file in the mount (absent from the manifest) is REFUSED, and so is a manifest
   entry with no file.
6. an existing destination file is REFUSED (`O_EXCL` semantics) and its bytes are unchanged.
7. a symlinked destination is REFUSED **and the sentinel file behind the symlink is byte-identical
   afterwards**.
8. a manifest that is itself a symlink, or a member that escapes the mount root, is REFUSED.
9. a non-UTF-8 / non-text member type is REFUSED.
10. the refusal path is a **non-zero exit** through the module's CLI `main()` equivalent, and the
    output above the cap is refused rather than trimmed.

+def _is_text_member(data: bytes) -> bool:
+    """A member is embeddable verbatim only if it is UTF-8 text with no NUL byte.
+
+    The fallback document is markdown, so a non-text member could only be embedded through a lossy
+    ``decode(..., "replace")`` that silently corrupts the source bytes. Fail closed instead.
+    """
+    if b"\x00" in data:
+        return False
+    try:
+        data.decode("utf-8")
+    except UnicodeDecodeError:
+        return False
+    return True
+

+"""Stage B lane B2: the Web fallback single-document projection.
+
+Exercises ``tools/build_web_fallback.py`` end to end against temp-directory mount packs. Nothing
+here touches the network or the real repository tree: every fixture is authored under a
+``tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`` and every pack is a small ``MANIFEST.sha256`` plus its members.
+
+The tool reproduces one frozen mount pack into ONE bounded markdown document
+(``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY``) and is fail-closed. The cases below pin the positive exact projection and the
+refusals:
+
+ 1. exact projection: verbatim member bytes, member inventory table, ``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY`` stamp
+ 2. stale release stamp (only the release id, or only the pinned commit, is REFUSED)
+ 3. over-cap composition REFUSED, and the destination is never created (no truncation)
+ 4. member digest disagreeing with ``MANIFEST.sha256`` REFUSED
+ 5. an unexpected extra file REFUSED; a manifest entry with no file REFUSED
+ 6. an existing destination REFUSED with its bytes unchanged (``O_EXCL``)
+ 7. a symlinked destination REFUSED, with the file behind it byte-identical
+ 8. a symlinked manifest / symlinked member REFUSED; a member path escaping the root REFUSED
+ 9. a non-UTF-8 / non-text member REFUSED
+10. the CLI ``main()`` refusal path exits non-zero and refuses above-cap output instead of trimming
+
+The fixtures are authored as LF-only UTF-8, which is exactly the canonical byte sequence the pack
+builder ``tools/build_mount_pack.py`` hashes (EOL-normalised text members), so a member's manifest
+digest is simply ``sha256`` of the bytes written here.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import hashlib
+import io
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+for _entry in (str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "src")):
+    if _entry not in sys.path:
+        sys.path.insert(0, _entry)
+
+from tools import build_web_fallback as WFB  # noqa: E402
+
+# Call the module's real entry point exactly once, resolved by name. The brief names it ``build()``;
+# the tool currently exposes ``build_fallback()``. Never a re-implementation.
+build = getattr(WFB, "build", None) or WFB.build_fallback
+
+RELEASE_ID = "v0.1.1-preview.3"
+RELEASE_COMMIT = "9f1c0b3d5e7a2468ac5df1b9c3e70d4f6a8b0c2e"
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- fixture helpers
+
+def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _manifest_text(entries: list[tuple[str, bytes]]) -> str:
+    return "".join(f"{_sha256(data)}  {rel}\n" for rel, data in entries)
+
+
+def _write_pack(root: Path, members: dict[str, bytes], *, manifest: str | None = None) -> Path:
+    """Author a mount pack: member files (LF bytes verbatim) plus a derived ``MANIFEST.sha256``."""
+    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    for rel, data in members.items():
+        member = root / rel
+        member.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        member.write_bytes(data)
+    text = manifest if manifest is not None else _manifest_text(list(members.items()))
+    (root / WFB.MANIFEST_NAME).write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
+    return root
+
+
+def _stamp(name: str, extra: str = "") -> bytes:
+    """A member document carrying BOTH the pinned release id and the pinned commit."""
+    text = (f"# {name}\n\n"
+            f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}\n"
+            f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}\n\n"
+            f"Verbatim body for {name}.\n{extra}")
+    return text.encode("utf-8")
+
+
+_SYMLINK_PROBE: list = [None]
+
+
+def _symlinks_supported() -> bool:
+    """Whether this host can actually create a symlink (Windows often cannot without privilege)."""
+    if _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] is None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            target = Path(tmp) / "target"
+            target.write_bytes(b"x")
+            link = Path(tmp) / "link"
+            try:
+                os.symlink(target, link)
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = os.path.islink(link)
+            except (OSError, NotImplementedError, AttributeError):
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = False
+    return bool(_SYMLINK_PROBE[0])
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _seam_symlink(path: Path):
+    """Report exactly ``path`` as a symlink through the tool's documented ``_path_is_symlink`` seam.
+
+    Used only when the host cannot create a real symlink; the refusal gate itself is unchanged.
+    """
+    seam_path = os.path.abspath(str(path))
+    real = WFB._path_is_symlink
+
+    def fake(candidate):
+        return os.path.abspath(str(candidate)) == seam_path or real(candidate)
+
+    WFB._path_is_symlink = fake
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        WFB._path_is_symlink = real
+
+
+class WebFallbackTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self._td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(self._td.cleanup)
+        self.td = Path(self._td.name)
+
+    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- fixtures
+
+    def members(self) -> dict[str, bytes]:
+        return {
+            "PIPD_A.md": _stamp("PIPD_A.md", "Alpha payload line.\n"),
+            "references/PIPD_B.md": _stamp("PIPD_B.md", "Beta payload line.\n"),
+        }
+
+    def pack(self, members: dict[str, bytes] | None = None, *, manifest: str | None = None,
+             name: str = "pack") -> Path:
+        return _write_pack(self.td / name, members if members is not None else self.members(),
+                           manifest=manifest)
+
+    def build_pack(self, pack: Path, out: Path, *, size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP) -> dict:
+        return build(mount_pack=pack, release_id=RELEASE_ID, release_commit=RELEASE_COMMIT,
+                     out_path=out, size_cap=size_cap)
+
+    def assert_refused(self, pack: Path, out: Path, code: str, *,
+                       size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP):
+        with self.assertRaises(WFB.Refusal) as caught:
+            self.build_pack(pack, out, size_cap=size_cap)
+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, code, str(caught.exception))
+        self.assertFalse(out.exists(), "a refused build must not leave a destination behind")
+        return caught.exception
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------- 1. positive
+
+    def test_exact_projection_verbatim_inventory_and_ceiling_stamp(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        pack = self.pack(members)
+        out = self.td / "fallback.md"
+
+        report = self.build_pack(pack, out)
+
+        self.assertEqual(report["verdict"], "BUILT")
+        self.assertTrue(report["doc_mount_only"])
+        self.assertEqual(report["member_count"], len(members))
+        self.assertEqual(report["out"], str(out))
+        document = out.read_bytes()
+        self.assertEqual(len(document), report["bytes"])
+        self.assertEqual(_sha256(document), report["sha256"])
+
+        # ONE markdown document, and nothing else beside it.
+        self.assertEqual([p.name for p in self.td.iterdir() if p.is_file()], ["fallback.md"])
+
+        text = document.decode("utf-8")
+        self.assertIn(WFB.FALLBACK_SCHEMA, text)
+        self.assertIn("DOC_MOUNT_ONLY", text)
+        self.assertIn(f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}", text)
+        self.assertIn(f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}", text)
+        self.assertIn("## Member inventory", text)
+
+        for rel, data in members.items():
+            # inventory table row, keyed by the manifest digest
+            self.assertIn(f"| {rel} | {_sha256(data)} |", text)
+            # embedded section carries the source bytes verbatim
+            self.assertIn(data, document)
+            begin = f"<!-- BEGIN MEMBER {rel} -->\n"
+            end = f"\n<!-- END MEMBER {rel} -->"
+            start = text.index(begin) + len(begin)
+            stop = text.index(end, start)
+            self.assertEqual(text[start:stop].encode("utf-8"), data,
+                             f"{rel} was not embedded verbatim")
+
+        # Deterministic: the same inputs produce byte-identical documents (no timestamp anywhere).
+        again = self.td / "fallback-again.md"
+        self.build_pack(pack, again)
+        self.assertEqual(out.read_bytes(), again.read_bytes())

+    # ------------------------------------------------------- 2. stale release stamp
+
+    def test_stale_stamp_release_without_pinned_commit_refused(self):

+        self.assert_refused(pack, self.td / "stale-b.md", "RELEASE_STAMP_MISSING")

+    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- 3. over cap

+    def test_over_cap_refused_with_no_destination_and_no_truncation(self):

+"""Stage B lane B2: the Web fallback single-document projection.
+
+Exercises ``tools/build_web_fallback.py`` end to end against temp-directory mount packs. Nothing
+here touches the network or the real repository tree: every fixture is authored under a
+``tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`` and every pack is a small ``MANIFEST.sha256`` plus its members.
+
+The tool reproduces one frozen mount pack into ONE bounded markdown document
+(``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY``) and is fail-closed. The cases below pin the positive exact projection and the
+refusals:
+
+ 1. exact projection: verbatim member bytes, member inventory table, ``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY`` stamp
+ 2. stale release stamp (only the release id, or only the pinned commit, is REFUSED)
+ 3. over-cap composition REFUSED, and the destination is never created (no truncation)
+ 4. member digest disagreeing with ``MANIFEST.sha256`` REFUSED
+ 5. an unexpected extra file REFUSED; a manifest entry with no file REFUSED
+ 6. an existing destination REFUSED with its bytes unchanged (``O_EXCL``)
+ 7. a symlinked destination REFUSED, with the file behind it byte-identical
+ 8. a symlinked manifest / symlinked member REFUSED; a member path escaping the root REFUSED
+ 9. a non-UTF-8 / non-text member REFUSED
+10. the CLI ``main()`` refusal path exits non-zero and refuses above-cap output instead of trimming
+
+The fixtures are authored as LF-only UTF-8, which is exactly the canonical byte sequence the pack
+builder ``tools/build_mount_pack.py`` hashes (EOL-normalised text members), so a member's manifest
+digest is simply ``sha256`` of the bytes written here.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import hashlib
+import io
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+for _entry in (str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "src")):
+    if _entry not in sys.path:
+        sys.path.insert(0, _entry)
+
+from tools import build_web_fallback as WFB  # noqa: E402
+
+# Call the module's real entry point exactly once, resolved by name. The brief names it ``build()``;
+# the tool currently exposes ``build_fallback()``. Never a re-implementation.
+build = getattr(WFB, "build", None) or WFB.build_fallback
+
+RELEASE_ID = "v0.1.1-preview.3"
+RELEASE_COMMIT = "9f1c0b3d5e7a2468ac5df1b9c3e70d4f6a8b0c2e"
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- fixture helpers
+
+def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _manifest_text(entries: list[tuple[str, bytes]]) -> str:
+    return "".join(f"{_sha256(data)}  {rel}\n" for rel, data in entries)
+
+
+def _write_pack(root: Path, members: dict[str, bytes], *, manifest: str | None = None) -> Path:
+    """Author a mount pack: member files (LF bytes verbatim) plus a derived ``MANIFEST.sha256``."""
+    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    for rel, data in members.items():
+        member = root / rel
+        member.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        member.write_bytes(data)
+    text = manifest if manifest is not None else _manifest_text(list(members.items()))
+    (root / WFB.MANIFEST_NAME).write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
+    return root
+
+
+def _stamp(name: str, extra: str = "") -> bytes:
+    """A member document carrying BOTH the pinned release id and the pinned commit."""
+    text = (f"# {name}\n\n"
+            f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}\n"
+            f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}\n\n"
+            f"Verbatim body for {name}.\n{extra}")
+    return text.encode("utf-8")
+
+
+_SYMLINK_PROBE: list = [None]
+
+
+def _symlinks_supported() -> bool:
+    """Whether this host can actually create a symlink (Windows often cannot without privilege)."""
+    if _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] is None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            target = Path(tmp) / "target"
+            target.write_bytes(b"x")
+            link = Path(tmp) / "link"
+            try:
+                os.symlink(target, link)
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = os.path.islink(link)
+            except (OSError, NotImplementedError, AttributeError):
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = False
+    return bool(_SYMLINK_PROBE[0])
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _seam_symlink(path: Path):
+    """Report exactly ``path`` as a symlink through the tool's documented ``_path_is_symlink`` seam.
+
+    Used only when the host cannot create a real symlink; the refusal gate itself is unchanged.
+    """
+    seam_path = os.path.abspath(str(path))
+    real = WFB._path_is_symlink
+
+    def fake(candidate):
+        return os.path.abspath(str(candidate)) == seam_path or real(candidate)
+
+    WFB._path_is_symlink = fake
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        WFB._path_is_symlink = real
+
+
+class WebFallbackTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self._td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(self._td.cleanup)
+        self.td = Path(self._td.name)
+
+    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- fixtures
+
+    def members(self) -> dict[str, bytes]:
+        return {
+            "PIPD_A.md": _stamp("PIPD_A.md", "Alpha payload line.\n"),
+            "references/PIPD_B.md": _stamp("PIPD_B.md", "Beta payload line.\n"),
+        }
+
+    def pack(self, members: dict[str, bytes] | None = None, *, manifest: str | None = None,
+             name: str = "pack") -> Path:
+        return _write_pack(self.td / name, members if members is not None else self.members(),
+                           manifest=manifest)
+
+    def build_pack(self, pack: Path, out: Path, *, size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP) -> dict:
+        return build(mount_pack=pack, release_id=RELEASE_ID, release_commit=RELEASE_COMMIT,
+                     out_path=out, size_cap=size_cap)
+
+    def assert_refused(self, pack: Path, out: Path, code: str, *,
+                       size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP):
+        with self.assertRaises(WFB.Refusal) as caught:
+            self.build_pack(pack, out, size_cap=size_cap)
+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, code, str(caught.exception))
+        self.assertFalse(out.exists(), "a refused build must not leave a destination behind")
+        return caught.exception
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------- 1. positive
+
+    def test_exact_projection_verbatim_inventory_and_ceiling_stamp(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        pack = self.pack(members)
+        out = self.td / "fallback.md"
+
+        report = self.build_pack(pack, out)
+
+        self.assertEqual(report["verdict"], "BUILT")
+        self.assertTrue(report["doc_mount_only"])
+        self.assertEqual(report["member_count"], len(members))
+        self.assertEqual(report["out"], str(out))
+        document = out.read_bytes()
+        self.assertEqual(len(document), report["bytes"])
+        self.assertEqual(_sha256(document), report["sha256"])
+
+        # ONE markdown document, and nothing else beside it.
+        self.assertEqual([p.name for p in self.td.iterdir() if p.is_file()], ["fallback.md"])
+
+        text = document.decode("utf-8")
+        self.assertIn(WFB.FALLBACK_SCHEMA, text)
+        self.assertIn("DOC_MOUNT_ONLY", text)
+        self.assertIn(f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}", text)
+        self.assertIn(f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}", text)
+        self.assertIn("## Member inventory", text)
+
+        for rel, data in members.items():
+            # inventory table row, keyed by the manifest digest
+            self.assertIn(f"| {rel} | {_sha256(data)} |", text)
+            # embedded section carries the source bytes verbatim
+            self.assertIn(data, document)
+            begin = f"<!-- BEGIN MEMBER {rel} -->\n"
+            end = f"\n<!-- END MEMBER {rel} -->"
+            start = text.index(begin) + len(begin)
+            stop = text.index(end, start)
+            self.assertEqual(text[start:stop].encode("utf-8"), data,
+                             f"{rel} was not embedded verbatim")
+
+        # Deterministic: the same inputs produce byte-identical documents (no timestamp anywhere).
+        again = self.td / "fallback-again.md"
+        self.build_pack(pack, again)
+        self.assertEqual(out.read_bytes(), again.read_bytes())
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------- 2. stale release stamp
+
+    def test_stale_stamp_release_without_pinned_commit_refused(self):

+    def test_over_cap_refused_with_no_destination_and_no_truncation(self):

+def _is_text_member(data: bytes) -> bool:
+    """A member is embeddable verbatim only if it is UTF-8 text with no NUL byte.
+
+    The fallback document is markdown, so a non-text member could only be embedded through a lossy
+    ``decode(..., "replace")`` that silently corrupts the source bytes. Fail closed instead.
+    """
+    if b"\x00" in data:
+        return False
+    try:
+        data.decode("utf-8")
+    except UnicodeDecodeError:
+        return False
+    return True

+"""Stage B lane B2: the Web fallback single-document projection.
+
+Exercises ``tools/build_web_fallback.py`` end to end against temp-directory mount packs. Nothing
+here touches the network or the real repository tree: every fixture is authored under a
+``tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`` and every pack is a small ``MANIFEST.sha256`` plus its members.
+
+The tool reproduces one frozen mount pack into ONE bounded markdown document
+(``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY``) and is fail-closed. The cases below pin the positive exact projection and the
+refusals:
+
+ 1. exact projection: verbatim member bytes, member inventory table, ``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY`` stamp
+ 2. stale release stamp (only the release id, or only the pinned commit, is REFUSED)
+ 3. over-cap composition REFUSED, and the destination is never created (no truncation)
+ 4. member digest disagreeing with ``MANIFEST.sha256`` REFUSED
+ 5. an unexpected extra file REFUSED; a manifest entry with no file REFUSED
+ 6. an existing destination REFUSED with its bytes unchanged (``O_EXCL``)
+ 7. a symlinked destination REFUSED, with the file behind it byte-identical
+ 8. a symlinked manifest / symlinked member REFUSED; a member path escaping the root REFUSED
+ 9. a non-UTF-8 / non-text member REFUSED
+10. the CLI ``main()`` refusal path exits non-zero and refuses above-cap output instead of trimming
+
+The fixtures are authored as LF-only UTF-8, which is exactly the canonical byte sequence the pack
+builder ``tools/build_mount_pack.py`` hashes (EOL-normalised text members), so a member's manifest
+digest is simply ``sha256`` of the bytes written here.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import hashlib
+import io
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+for _entry in (str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "src")):
+    if _entry not in sys.path:
+        sys.path.insert(0, _entry)
+
+from tools import build_web_fallback as WFB  # noqa: E402
+
+# Call the module's real entry point exactly once, resolved by name. The brief names it ``build()``;
+# the tool currently exposes ``build_fallback()``. Never a re-implementation.
+build = getattr(WFB, "build", None) or WFB.build_fallback
+
+RELEASE_ID = "v0.1.1-preview.3"
+RELEASE_COMMIT = "9f1c0b3d5e7a2468ac5df1b9c3e70d4f6a8b0c2e"
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- fixture helpers
+
+def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _manifest_text(entries: list[tuple[str, bytes]]) -> str:
+    return "".join(f"{_sha256(data)}  {rel}\n" for rel, data in entries)
+
+
+def _write_pack(root: Path, members: dict[str, bytes], *, manifest: str | None = None) -> Path:
+    """Author a mount pack: member files (LF bytes verbatim) plus a derived ``MANIFEST.sha256``."""
+    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    for rel, data in members.items():
+        member = root / rel
+        member.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        member.write_bytes(data)
+    text = manifest if manifest is not None else _manifest_text(list(members.items()))
+    (root / WFB.MANIFEST_NAME).write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
+    return root
+
+
+def _stamp(name: str, extra: str = "") -> bytes:
+    """A member document carrying BOTH the pinned release id and the pinned commit."""
+    text = (f"# {name}\n\n"
+            f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}\n"
+            f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}\n\n"
+            f"Verbatim body for {name}.\n{extra}")
+    return text.encode("utf-8")
+
+
+_SYMLINK_PROBE: list = [None]
+
+
+def _symlinks_supported() -> bool:
+    """Whether this host can actually create a symlink (Windows often cannot without privilege)."""
+    if _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] is None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            target = Path(tmp) / "target"
+            target.write_bytes(b"x")
+            link = Path(tmp) / "link"
+            try:
+                os.symlink(target, link)
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = os.path.islink(link)
+            except (OSError, NotImplementedError, AttributeError):
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = False
+    return bool(_SYMLINK_PROBE[0])
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _seam_symlink(path: Path):
+    """Report exactly ``path`` as a symlink through the tool's documented ``_path_is_symlink`` seam.
+
+    Used only when the host cannot create a real symlink; the refusal gate itself is unchanged.
+    """
+    seam_path = os.path.abspath(str(path))
+    real = WFB._path_is_symlink
+
+    def fake(candidate):
+        return os.path.abspath(str(candidate)) == seam_path or real(candidate)
+
+    WFB._path_is_symlink = fake
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        WFB._path_is_symlink = real
+

+    def members(self) -> dict[str, bytes]:
+        return {

+            "references/PIPD_B.md": _stamp("PIPD_B.md", "Beta payload line.\n"),
+        }

+    def pack(self, members: dict[str, bytes] | None = None, *, manifest: str | None = None,
+             name: str = "pack") -> Path:
+        return _write_pack(self.td / name, members if members is not None else self.members(),
+                           manifest=manifest)

+    def build_pack(self, pack: Path, out: Path, *, size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP) -> dict:
+        return build(mount_pack=pack, release_id=RELEASE_ID, release_commit=RELEASE_COMMIT,

+        with self.assertRaises(WFB.Refusal) as caught:

+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, code, str(caught.exception))
+        self.assertFalse(out.exists(), "a refused build must not leave a destination behind")
+        return caught.exception

+def _is_text_member(data: bytes) -> bool:
+    """A member is embeddable verbatim only if it is UTF-8 text with no NUL byte.
+
+    The fallback document is markdown, so a non-text member could only be embedded through a lossy
+    ``decode(..., "replace")`` that silently corrupts the source bytes. Fail closed instead.
+    """
+    if b"\x00" in data:
+        return False
+    try:
+        data.decode("utf-8")
+    except UnicodeDecodeError:
+        return False
+    return True

+"""Stage B lane B2: the Web fallback single-document projection.
+
+Exercises ``tools/build_web_fallback.py`` end to end against temp-directory mount packs. Nothing
+here touches the network or the real repository tree: every fixture is authored under a
+``tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`` and every pack is a small ``MANIFEST.sha256`` plus its members.
+
+The tool reproduces one frozen mount pack into ONE bounded markdown document
+(``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY``) and is fail-closed. The cases below pin the positive exact projection and the
+refusals:
+
+ 1. exact projection: verbatim member bytes, member inventory table, ``DOC_MOUNT_ONLY`` stamp
+ 2. stale release stamp (only the release id, or only the pinned commit, is REFUSED)
+ 3. over-cap composition REFUSED, and the destination is never created (no truncation)
+ 4. member digest disagreeing with ``MANIFEST.sha256`` REFUSED
+ 5. an unexpected extra file REFUSED; a manifest entry with no file REFUSED
+ 6. an existing destination REFUSED with its bytes unchanged (``O_EXCL``)
+ 7. a symlinked destination REFUSED, with the file behind it byte-identical
+ 8. a symlinked manifest / symlinked member REFUSED; a member path escaping the root REFUSED
+ 9. a non-UTF-8 / non-text member REFUSED
+10. the CLI ``main()`` refusal path exits non-zero and refuses above-cap output instead of trimming
+
+The fixtures are authored as LF-only UTF-8, which is exactly the canonical byte sequence the pack
+builder ``tools/build_mount_pack.py`` hashes (EOL-normalised text members), so a member's manifest
+digest is simply ``sha256`` of the bytes written here.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import hashlib
+import io
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+for _entry in (str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "src")):
+    if _entry not in sys.path:
+        sys.path.insert(0, _entry)
+
+from tools import build_web_fallback as WFB  # noqa: E402
+
+# Call the module's real entry point exactly once, resolved by name. The brief names it ``build()``;
+# the tool currently exposes ``build_fallback()``. Never a re-implementation.
+build = getattr(WFB, "build", None) or WFB.build_fallback
+
+RELEASE_ID = "v0.1.1-preview.3"
+RELEASE_COMMIT = "9f1c0b3d5e7a2468ac5df1b9c3e70d4f6a8b0c2e"
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- fixture helpers
+
+def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _manifest_text(entries: list[tuple[str, bytes]]) -> str:
+    return "".join(f"{_sha256(data)}  {rel}\n" for rel, data in entries)
+
+
+def _write_pack(root: Path, members: dict[str, bytes], *, manifest: str | None = None) -> Path:
+    """Author a mount pack: member files (LF bytes verbatim) plus a derived ``MANIFEST.sha256``."""
+    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    for rel, data in members.items():
+        member = root / rel
+        member.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        member.write_bytes(data)
+    text = manifest if manifest is not None else _manifest_text(list(members.items()))
+    (root / WFB.MANIFEST_NAME).write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
+    return root
+
+
+def _stamp(name: str, extra: str = "") -> bytes:
+    """A member document carrying BOTH the pinned release id and the pinned commit."""
+    text = (f"# {name}\n\n"
+            f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}\n"
+            f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}\n\n"
+            f"Verbatim body for {name}.\n{extra}")
+    return text.encode("utf-8")
+
+
+_SYMLINK_PROBE: list = [None]
+
+
+def _symlinks_supported() -> bool:
+    """Whether this host can actually create a symlink (Windows often cannot without privilege)."""
+    if _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] is None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            target = Path(tmp) / "target"
+            target.write_bytes(b"x")
+            link = Path(tmp) / "link"
+            try:
+                os.symlink(target, link)
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = os.path.islink(link)
+            except (OSError, NotImplementedError, AttributeError):
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = False
+    return bool(_SYMLINK_PROBE[0])
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _seam_symlink(path: Path):
+    """Report exactly ``path`` as a symlink through the tool's documented ``_path_is_symlink`` seam.
+
+    Used only when the host cannot create a real symlink; the refusal gate itself is unchanged.
+    """
+    seam_path = os.path.abspath(str(path))
+    real = WFB._path_is_symlink
+
+    def fake(candidate):
+        return os.path.abspath(str(candidate)) == seam_path or real(candidate)
+
+    WFB._path_is_symlink = fake
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        WFB._path_is_symlink = real
+
+
+class WebFallbackTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self._td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(self._td.cleanup)
+        self.td = Path(self._td.name)
+
+    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- fixtures
+
+    def members(self) -> dict[str, bytes]:
+        return {
+            "PIPD_A.md": _stamp("PIPD_A.md", "Alpha payload line.\n"),
+            "references/PIPD_B.md": _stamp("PIPD_B.md", "Beta payload line.\n"),
+        }
+
+    def pack(self, members: dict[str, bytes] | None = None, *, manifest: str | None = None,
+             name: str = "pack") -> Path:
+        return _write_pack(self.td / name, members if members is not None else self.members(),
+                           manifest=manifest)
+
+    def build_pack(self, pack: Path, out: Path, *, size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP) -> dict:
+        return build(mount_pack=pack, release_id=RELEASE_ID, release_commit=RELEASE_COMMIT,
+                     out_path=out, size_cap=size_cap)
+
+    def assert_refused(self, pack: Path, out: Path, code: str, *,
+                       size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP):
+        with self.assertRaises(WFB.Refusal) as caught:
+            self.build_pack(pack, out, size_cap=size_cap)
+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, code, str(caught.exception))
+        self.assertFalse(out.exists(), "a refused build must not leave a destination behind")
+        return caught.exception
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------- 1. positive
+
+    def test_exact_projection_verbatim_inventory_and_ceiling_stamp(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        pack = self.pack(members)
+        out = self.td / "fallback.md"
+
+        report = self.build_pack(pack, out)
+
+        self.assertEqual(report["verdict"], "BUILT")
+        self.assertTrue(report["doc_mount_only"])
+        self.assertEqual(report["member_count"], len(members))
+        self.assertEqual(report["out"], str(out))
+        document = out.read_bytes()
+        self.assertEqual(len(document), report["bytes"])
+        self.assertEqual(_sha256(document), report["sha256"])
+
+        # ONE markdown document, and nothing else beside it.
+        self.assertEqual([p.name for p in self.td.iterdir() if p.is_file()], ["fallback.md"])
+
+        text = document.decode("utf-8")
+        self.assertIn(WFB.FALLBACK_SCHEMA, text)
+        self.assertIn("DOC_MOUNT_ONLY", text)
+        self.assertIn(f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}", text)
+        self.assertIn(f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}", text)
+        self.assertIn("## Member inventory", text)
+
+        for rel, data in members.items():
+            # inventory table row, keyed by the manifest digest
+            self.assertIn(f"| {rel} | {_sha256(data)} |", text)
+            # embedded section carries the source bytes verbatim
+            self.assertIn(data, document)
+            begin = f"<!-- BEGIN MEMBER {rel} -->\n"
+            end = f"\n<!-- END MEMBER {rel} -->"
+            start = text.index(begin) + len(begin)
+            stop = text.index(end, start)
+            self.assertEqual(text[start:stop].encode("utf-8"), data,
+                             f"{rel} was not embedded verbatim")
+
+        # Deterministic: the same inputs produce byte-identical documents (no timestamp anywhere).
+        again = self.td / "fallback-again.md"
+        self.build_pack(pack, again)
+        self.assertEqual(out.read_bytes(), again.read_bytes())
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------- 2. stale release stamp
+
+    def test_stale_stamp_release_without_pinned_commit_refused(self):
+        doc = (f"# Doc\n\n- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}\n\nno pinned commit here\n").encode("utf-8")
+        pack = self.pack({"PIPD_A.md": doc}, name="pack-stale-a")
+        self.assert_refused(pack, self.td / "stale-a.md", "RELEASE_STAMP_MISSING")
+
+    def test_stale_stamp_pinned_commit_without_release_refused(self):
+        doc = (f"# Doc\n\n- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}\n\nno release id here\n").encode("utf-8")
+        pack = self.pack({"PIPD_A.md": doc}, name="pack-stale-b")
+        self.assert_refused(pack, self.td / "stale-b.md", "RELEASE_STAMP_MISSING")
+
+    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- 3. over cap
+
+    def test_over_cap_refused_with_no_destination_and_no_truncation(self):
+        pack = self.pack()
+        out = self.td / "overflow.md"
+        exc = self.assert_refused(pack, out, "SIZE_CAP_EXCEEDED", size_cap=64)
+        self.assertIn("refusing to truncate", exc.detail)
+        self.assertFalse(out.exists(), "an over-cap build must not truncate a prefix to disk")
+
+    # -------------------------------------------------------------- 4. digest mismatch
+
+    def test_member_digest_mismatch_refused(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        manifest = (f"{_sha256(members['PIPD_A.md'])}  PIPD_A.md\n"
+                    f"{'0' * 64}  references/PIPD_B.md\n")
+        pack = self.pack(members, manifest=manifest, name="pack-digest")
+        self.assert_refused(pack, self.td / "digest.md", "MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH")
+
+    # ---------------------------------------------- 5. extra file / manifest entry missing
+
+    def test_unexpected_extra_file_refused(self):
+        pack = self.pack()
+        (pack / "EXTRA.md").write_bytes(b"# a file the manifest never listed\n")
+        self.assert_refused(pack, self.td / "extra.md", "UNEXPECTED_EXTRA_FILE")
+
+    def test_manifest_entry_without_file_refused(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        manifest = _manifest_text(list(members.items()))
+        pack = _write_pack(self.td / "pack-missing",
+                           {"PIPD_A.md": members["PIPD_A.md"]}, manifest=manifest)
+        self.assert_refused(pack, self.td / "missing.md", "MANIFEST_MEMBER_MISSING")
+
+    # -------------------------------------------------------- 6. destination exists
+
+    def test_existing_destination_refused_and_bytes_unchanged(self):
+        pack = self.pack()
+        out = self.td / "exists.md"
+        before = b"# pre-existing document\nkeep every byte\n"
+        out.write_bytes(before)
+        with self.assertRaises(WFB.Refusal) as caught:
+            self.build_pack(pack, out)
+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, "DESTINATION_EXISTS")
+        self.assertEqual(out.read_bytes(), before, "O_EXCL must never overwrite the destination")
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------- 7. symlinked destination
+
+    def test_symlinked_destination_refused_and_target_byte_identical(self):
+        pack = self.pack()
+        sentinel = self.td / "sentinel.md"
+        sentinel_bytes = b"# sentinel behind the symlink\nmust stay byte-identical\n"
+        sentinel.write_bytes(sentinel_bytes)
+        dest = self.td / "link.md"
+
+        if _symlinks_supported():
+            os.symlink(sentinel, dest)
+            ctx = contextlib.nullcontext()
+        else:
+            ctx = _seam_symlink(dest)  # the tool's own test seam; the gate code is unchanged
+        with ctx:
+            exc = self.assert_refused(pack, dest, "DESTINATION_SYMLINK")
+        self.assertIn("symlink", exc.detail)
+        self.assertEqual(sentinel.read_bytes(), sentinel_bytes,
+                         "the file behind the symlink must be untouched")
+        if _symlinks_supported():
+            self.assertTrue(os.path.islink(dest))
+        else:
+            self.assertFalse(dest.exists())
+
+    # ---------------------------- 8. symlinked manifest / symlinked member / path escape
+
+    def test_symlinked_manifest_refused(self):
+        pack = self.pack()
+        manifest = pack / WFB.MANIFEST_NAME
+        out = self.td / "manifest-link.md"
+        if _symlinks_supported():
+            target = self.td / "manifest-target.txt"
+            target.write_bytes(manifest.read_bytes())
+            manifest.unlink()
+            os.symlink(target, manifest)
+            ctx = contextlib.nullcontext()
+        else:
+            ctx = _seam_symlink(manifest)
+        with ctx:
+            self.assert_refused(pack, out, "MEMBER_SYMLINK")
+
+    def test_symlinked_member_refused(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        pack = self.pack(members)
+        member = pack / "references/PIPD_B.md"
+        out = self.td / "member-link.md"
+        if _symlinks_supported():
+            target = self.td / "member-target.md"
+            target.write_bytes(members["references/PIPD_B.md"])
+            member.unlink()
+            os.symlink(target, member)
+            ctx = contextlib.nullcontext()
+        else:
+            ctx = _seam_symlink(member)
+        with ctx:
+            self.assert_refused(pack, out, "MEMBER_SYMLINK")
+
+    def test_member_path_escaping_root_refused(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        escape_digest = _sha256(b"# outside\n")
+        manifest = _manifest_text(list(members.items())) + f"{escape_digest}  ../outside.md\n"
+        pack = self.pack(members, manifest=manifest, name="pack-escape")
+        self.assert_refused(pack, self.td / "escape.md", "PATH_ESCAPE")
+
+    # --------------------------------------------------------------- 9. non-text member
+
+    def test_non_utf8_member_refused(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        members["blob.bin"] = b"\xff\xfe\x00\x01\x80not utf-8 \xc3\x28\n"
+        pack = self.pack(members, name="pack-binary")
+        self.assert_refused(pack, self.td / "binary.md", "MEMBER_NOT_TEXT")
+
+    # --------------------------------------------------------- 10. CLI refusal path
+
+    def test_cli_refusal_is_nonzero_and_above_cap_is_refused_not_trimmed(self):
+        pack = self.pack()
+        out = self.td / "cli-overflow.md"
+        argv = ["--mount-pack", str(pack), "--release-id", RELEASE_ID,
+                "--release-commit", RELEASE_COMMIT, "--size-cap", "64", "--out", str(out)]
+        stdout = io.StringIO()
+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout):
+            rc = WFB.main(argv)
+        self.assertNotEqual(rc, 0, "a refusal must exit non-zero through main()")
+        self.assertIn("SIZE_CAP_EXCEEDED", stdout.getvalue())
+        self.assertFalse(out.exists(), "above-cap output must be refused, never trimmed")
+
+    def test_cli_refusal_is_nonzero_for_a_stale_stamp(self):
+        doc = (f"# Doc\n\n- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}\n\nstale, no commit\n").encode("utf-8")
+        pack = self.pack({"PIPD_A.md": doc}, name="pack-cli-stale")
+        out = self.td / "cli-stale.md"
+        stdout = io.StringIO()
+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout):
+            rc = WFB.main(["--mount-pack", str(pack), "--release-id", RELEASE_ID,
+                           "--release-commit", RELEASE_COMMIT, "--out", str(out)])
+        self.assertNotEqual(rc, 0)
+        self.assertIn("RELEASE_STAMP_MISSING", stdout.getvalue())
+        self.assertFalse(out.exists())
+
+    def test_cli_builds_when_the_pack_is_clean(self):
+        pack = self.pack()
+        out = self.td / "cli-ok.md"
+        stdout = io.StringIO()
+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout):
+            rc = WFB.main(["--mount-pack", str(pack), "--release-id", RELEASE_ID,
+                           "--release-commit", RELEASE_COMMIT, "--out", str(out)])
+        self.assertEqual(rc, 0, stdout.getvalue())
+        self.assertIn("DOC_MOUNT_ONLY", stdout.getvalue())
+        self.assertTrue(out.is_file())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+def _is_text_member(data: bytes) -> bool:
+    """A member is embeddable verbatim only if it is UTF-8 text with no NUL byte.
+
+    The fallback document is markdown, so a non-text member could only be embedded through a lossy
+    ``decode(..., "replace")`` that silently corrupts the source bytes. Fail closed instead.
+    """
+    if b"\x00" in data:
+        return False
+    try:
+        data.decode("utf-8")
+    except UnicodeDecodeError:
+        return False
+    return True

+here touches the network or the real repository tree: every fixture is authored under a

+ 7. a symlinked destination REFUSED, with the file behind it byte-identical

+ 9. a non-UTF-8 / non-text member REFUSED
+10. the CLI ``main()`` refusal path exits non-zero and refuses above-cap output instead of trimming

+builder ``tools/build_mount_pack.py`` hashes (EOL-normalised text members), so a member's manifest
+digest is simply ``sha256`` of the bytes written here.

+

+    return "".join(f"{_sha256(data)}  {rel}\n" for rel, data in entries)

+def _write_pack(root: Path, members: dict[str, bytes], *, manifest: str | None = None) -> Path:
+    """Author a mount pack: member files (LF bytes verbatim) plus a derived ``MANIFEST.sha256``."""
+    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    for rel, data in members.items():

+        member.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        member.write_bytes(data)
+    text = manifest if manifest is not None else _manifest_text(list(members.items()))
+    (root / WFB.MANIFEST_NAME).write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
+    return root
+
+
+def _stamp(name: str, extra: str = "") -> bytes:
+    """A member document carrying BOTH the pinned release id and the pinned commit."""
+    text = (f"# {name}\n\n"
+            f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}\n"
+            f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}\n\n"
+            f"Verbatim body for {name}.\n{extra}")
+    return text.encode("utf-8")
+
+
+_SYMLINK_PROBE: list = [None]
+
+
+def _symlinks_supported() -> bool:
+    """Whether this host can actually create a symlink (Windows often cannot without privilege)."""
+    if _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] is None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            target = Path(tmp) / "target"
+            target.write_bytes(b"x")
+            link = Path(tmp) / "link"
+            try:
+                os.symlink(target, link)
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = os.path.islink(link)
+            except (OSError, NotImplementedError, AttributeError):
+                _SYMLINK_PROBE[0] = False
+    return bool(_SYMLINK_PROBE[0])
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _seam_symlink(path: Path):
+    """Report exactly ``path`` as a symlink through the tool's documented ``_path_is_symlink`` seam.
+
+    Used only when the host cannot create a real symlink; the refusal gate itself is unchanged.
+    """
+    seam_path = os.path.abspath(str(path))
+    real = WFB._path_is_symlink
+
+    def fake(candidate):
+        return os.path.abspath(str(candidate)) == seam_path or real(candidate)
+
+    WFB._path_is_symlink = fake
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        WFB._path_is_symlink = real
+
+
+class WebFallbackTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self._td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(self._td.cleanup)
+        self.td = Path(self._td.name)
+
+    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- fixtures
+
+    def members(self) -> dict[str, bytes]:
+        return {
+            "PIPD_A.md": _stamp("PIPD_A.md", "Alpha payload line.\n"),
+            "references/PIPD_B.md": _stamp("PIPD_B.md", "Beta payload line.\n"),
+        }
+
+    def pack(self, members: dict[str, bytes] | None = None, *, manifest: str | None = None,
+             name: str = "pack") -> Path:
+        return _write_pack(self.td / name, members if members is not None else self.members(),
+                           manifest=manifest)
+
+    def build_pack(self, pack: Path, out: Path, *, size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP) -> dict:
+        return build(mount_pack=pack, release_id=RELEASE_ID, release_commit=RELEASE_COMMIT,
+                     out_path=out, size_cap=size_cap)
+
+    def assert_refused(self, pack: Path, out: Path, code: str, *,
+                       size_cap: int = WFB.DEFAULT_SIZE_CAP):
+        with self.assertRaises(WFB.Refusal) as caught:
+            self.build_pack(pack, out, size_cap=size_cap)
+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, code, str(caught.exception))
+        self.assertFalse(out.exists(), "a refused build must not leave a destination behind")
+        return caught.exception
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------- 1. positive
+
+    def test_exact_projection_verbatim_inventory_and_ceiling_stamp(self):
+        members = self.members()
+        pack = self.pack(members)
+        out = self.td / "fallback.md"
+
+        report = self.build_pack(pack, out)
+
+        self.assertEqual(report["verdict"], "BUILT")
+        self.assertTrue(report["doc_mount_only"])
+        self.assertEqual(report["member_count"], len(members))
+        self.assertEqual(report["out"], str(out))
+        document = out.read_bytes()
+        self.assertEqual(len(document), report["bytes"])
+        self.assertEqual(_sha256(document), report["sha256"])
+
+        # ONE markdown document, and nothing else beside it.
+        self.assertEqual([p.name for p in self.td.iterdir() if p.is_file()], ["fallback.md"])
+
+        text = document.decode("utf-8")
+        self.assertIn(WFB.FALLBACK_SCHEMA, text)
+        self.assertIn("DOC_MOUNT_ONLY", text)
+        self.assertIn(f"- release_id: {RELEASE_ID}", text)
+        self.assertIn(f"- release_commit: {RELEASE_COMMIT}", text)
+        self.assertIn("## Member inventory", text)
+
+        for rel, data in members.items():
+            # inventory table row, keyed by the manifest digest
+            self.assertIn(f"| {rel} | {_sha256(data)} |", text)
+            # embedded section carries the source bytes verbatim
+            self.assertIn(data, document)
+            begin = f"<!-- BEGIN MEMBER {rel} -->\n"
+            end = f"\n<!-- END MEMBER {rel} -->"
+            start = text.index(begin) + len(begin)
+            stop = text.index(end, start)
+            self.assertEqual(text[start:stop].encode("utf-8"), data,
+                             f"{rel} was not embedded verbatim")
+
+        # Deterministic: the same inputs produce byte-identical documents (no timestamp anywhere).
+        again = self.td / "fallback-again.md"
+        self.build_pack(pack, again)
+        self.assertEqual(out.read_bytes(), again.read_bytes())
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------- 2. stale release stamp

+def _is_text_member(data: bytes) -> bool:
+    """A member is embeddable verbatim only if it is UTF-8 text with no NUL byte.
+
+    The fallback document is markdown, so a non-text member could only be embedded through a lossy
+    ``decode(..., "replace")`` that silently corrupts the source bytes. Fail closed instead.
+    """
+    if b"\x00" in data:
+        return False
+    try:
+        data.decode("utf-8")
+    except UnicodeDecodeError:
+        return False
+    return True
