def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _read_zip(path: Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zf:
        return {n: zf.read(n) for n in zf.namelist()}


def _write_zip(path: Path, members: dict[str, bytes]) -> None:
    """Rewrite a zip deterministically, preserving the tool's fixed per-member stamp."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for name, data in members.items():
            info = zipfile.ZipInfo(name, date_time=BMP.FIXED_DATE_TIME)
            info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
            info.external_attr = 0o644 << 16
            info.create_system = 0
            zf.writestr(info, data)


class MountPackBuildTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.td = Path(self._td.name)

    def tearDown(self):
        self._td.cleanup()

    def _build(self, name="pack") -> Path:
        pack = self.td / PACK_NAME
        if not pack.exists():
            shutil.copytree(PACK_ROOT, pack)
        out = self.td / f"{name}.zip"
        BMP.build_pack(pack, out)
        return out

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- positive

    def test_pack_directory_has_exact_expected_files(self):
        present = {p.relative_to(PACK_ROOT).as_posix() for p in PACK_ROOT.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
        self.assertEqual(present, set(CONTENT_FILES) | {BMP.MANIFEST_NAME})

    def test_build_is_byte_deterministic(self):
        a = self._build("a")
        b = self._build("b")
        self.assertEqual(a.read_bytes(), b.read_bytes(), "same inputs must yield identical ZIP bytes")

    def test_verify_passes_and_names_nothing(self):
        out = self._build()
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertTrue(ok, problems)
        self.assertEqual(problems, [])

    def test_manifest_recomputes_from_members(self):
        out = self._build()
        members = _read_zip(out)
        manifest = members[f"{PACK_NAME}/{BMP.MANIFEST_NAME}"].decode("utf-8")
        entries = {
            rel: digest
            for digest, rel in (line.split("  ", 1) for line in manifest.splitlines() if line.strip())
        }
        self.assertEqual(set(entries), set(CONTENT_FILES))
        for rel in CONTENT_FILES:
            self.assertEqual(entries[rel], _sha256(members[f"{PACK_NAME}/{rel}"]))
        self.assertEqual(list(entries), sorted(entries))

    def test_manifest_is_last_archive_entry(self):
        out = self._build()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(out) as zf:
            names = zf.namelist()
        self.assertEqual(names[-1], f"{PACK_NAME}/{BMP.MANIFEST_NAME}")
        first_entry_rel = (_read_zip(out)[f"{PACK_NAME}/{BMP.MANIFEST_NAME}"]
                           .decode("utf-8").splitlines()[0].split("  ", 1)[1])
        self.assertNotEqual(first_entry_rel, BMP.MANIFEST_NAME)

    def test_all_members_are_stamped_fixed(self):
        out = self._build()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(out) as zf:
            for info in zf.infolist():
                self.assertEqual(info.date_time, BMP.FIXED_DATE_TIME)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ negatives

    def test_mutated_member_is_refused_and_named(self):
        out = self._build()
        members = _read_zip(out)
        target = f"{PACK_NAME}/references/PIPD_S4_CORE.md"
        members[target] = members[target] + b"\n<!-- tampered -->\n"
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("MUTATED_MEMBER: references/PIPD_S4_CORE.md", problems)

    def test_member_not_in_manifest_is_refused_and_named(self):
        out = self._build()
        members = _read_zip(out)
        members[f"{PACK_NAME}/EXTRA.md"] = b"leak\n"
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("UNMANIFESTED_FILE: EXTRA.md", problems)

    def test_manifest_entry_missing_from_zip_is_refused_and_named(self):
        out = self._build()
        members = _read_zip(out)
        del members[f"{PACK_NAME}/references/PIPD_EXAMPLES.md"]
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("MANIFEST_ENTRY_NOT_IN_ZIP: references/PIPD_EXAMPLES.md", problems)

    def test_path_escaping_pack_root_is_refused_and_named(self):
        out = self.td / "escape.zip"
        members = _read_zip(self._build())
        members["../evil.md"] = b"escape\n"
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("ESCAPES_PACK_ROOT: ../evil.md", problems)

    def test_absolute_path_is_refused(self):
        out = self.td / "abs.zip"
        members = _read_zip(self._build())
        members["/etc/evil.md"] = b"escape\n"
        _write_zip(out, members)
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(out)
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertIn("ESCAPES_PACK_ROOT: /etc/evil.md", problems)

    def test_verify_nonexistent_zip_refused(self):
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(self.td / "nope.zip")
        self.assertFalse(ok)
        self.assertTrue(any(p.startswith("ZIP_NOT_FOUND") for p in problems))

    # ------------------------------------------------ content requirements

    def test_every_document_carries_locator_and_release_identity(self):
        for rel in CONTENT_FILES:
            text = (PACK_ROOT / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIn(RELEASE_IDENTITY, text, f"{rel} lacks the release identity")
            self.assertIn(RELEASE_TAG_COMMIT, text, f"{rel} lacks the tag commit")
            self.assertIn("Source Locators", text, f"{rel} lacks a source locator section")

    def test_eight_existing_skills_and_no_ninth(self):
        index = (PACK_ROOT / "references/PIPD_8_SKILLS_INDEX.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for skill in ("pipd-route-intake", "pipd-authority-source", "pipd-profile-tailor",
                      "pipd-pi-compile", "pipd-pd-bind", "pipd-execution-contract",
                      "pipd-assurance-tqaep", "pipd-package-project"):
            self.assertIn(skill, index)
        dispatcher = (PACK_ROOT / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("dispatcher", dispatcher.lower())
        self.assertIn("not a ninth skill", dispatcher.lower())
        for skill in ("pipd-route-intake", "pipd-package-project"):
            self.assertIn(skill, dispatcher)

    def test_dispatcher_declares_triggers_and_non_triggers(self):
        text = (PACK_ROOT / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("## Trigger", text)
        self.assertIn("## Non-trigger", text)
        self.assertIn("chit-chat", text)
        for code in ("NO_SOURCE_LOCATOR", "MISSING_INPUT", "UNAUTHORISED_ACTION",
                     "S5_S6_NOT_AUTHORISED", "UNKNOWN_RISK_NOT_ASSESSED"):
            self.assertIn(code, text)

    def test_readme_mount_marks_unavailable_capabilities(self):
        text = (PACK_ROOT / "README_MOUNT.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for capability in ("tool execution", "repository writing", "CLI invocation",
                           "HITL authority", "network / file access"):
            self.assertIn(capability, text, f"README_MOUNT misses capability row: {capability}")
        self.assertGreaterEqual(text.count("NOT_AVAILABLE"), 5)
        self.assertIn("Plugins", text)
        self.assertIn("Create -> Upload", text)
        self.assertIn("did not exercise", text.lower())
        self.assertIn("external executor", text.lower())

    def test_quickstart_prompt_bounds_the_role(self):
        text = (PACK_ROOT / "PIPD_LS_SP_QUICKSTART_PROMPT.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        low = text.lower()
        self.assertIn("design assistant", low)
        for doc in ("SKILL.md", "PIPD_S4_CORE.md", "PIPD_SOURCE_MAP.md"):
            self.assertIn(doc, text)
        self.assertIn("executor", low)
        self.assertIn("typed refusal", low)
        self.assertIn("never fabricate", low)
        for part in ("SOURCE LOCATORS", "ACTUAL EVIDENCE", "CLAIM CEILING", "NEXT STEP"):
            self.assertIn(part, text)

    def test_pack_contains_no_obvious_secret(self):
        banned = re.compile(r"(gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|"
                            r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----)")
        for rel in CONTENT_FILES:
            text = (PACK_ROOT / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIsNone(banned.search(text), f"{rel} appears to contain a secret")

    # --------------------------------------------------- published artifact

    def test_published_zip_verifies_and_matches_sidecar(self):
        self.assertTrue(ZIP.is_file(), "the published ZIP is missing; run the build command")
        ok, problems = BMP.verify_pack(ZIP)
        self.assertTrue(ok, problems)
        digest = _sha256(ZIP.read_bytes())
        recorded = SIDECAR.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split()[0]
        self.assertEqual(digest, recorded)

    def test_uat_evidence_file_coverage(self):
        self.assertTrue(UAT.is_file(), "the UAT evidence file is missing")
        data = json.loads(UAT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        cases = {c["case_id"]: c for c in data["cases"]}
        self.assertEqual(len(cases), 5)
        for cid, case in cases.items():
            for key in ("fixed_input", "expected", "observed", "raw_output", "verdict",
                        "claim_ceiling"):
                self.assertIn(key, case, f"{cid} missing {key}")
            self.assertIn(case["verdict"], ("PASS", "FAIL", "NOT_SUPPORTED"))
        for cid, case in cases.items():
            if case["verdict"] != "PASS":
                self.assertEqual(case["verdict"], "NOT_SUPPORTED", cid)
                self.assertTrue(case.get("reason"), f"{cid} needs a reason")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""S4POST Stage B: freeze the eight public skill packs into a source ledger.

The public plugin builder (``build_public_plugin.py``) may only consume the eight ``skills/pipd-*``
packs through a frozen ledger produced here from a *clean checkout*. The ledger pins the repo, the
commit (40 hex), the tree (40 hex), the exact eight skill names and a ``path -> sha256`` for every
file under them, and it is the binding the owner derivation records must match
(``source_sha256``). This tool REFUSES (typed reason, non-zero exit) instead of warning:

  * ``DIRTY_WORKTREE``          git status --porcelain is not empty
  * ``NOT_REPO_ROOT``           the given root is not the git top-level
  * ``GIT_UNAVAILABLE`` / ``GIT_FAILED``  git could not run
  * ``WRONG_SKILL_SET``         the skills root is missing or carries an unexpected skill
  * ``SYMLINK_MEMBER``          a symlinked file or directory inside a skill
  * ``NON_REGULAR_FILE``        a special/irregular file inside a skill (FIFO, socket, ...)
  * ``HIDDEN_OR_SPECIAL_MEMBER`` a dot-file/dot-directory inside a skill
  * ``SKILLS_ROOT_MISSING``     the skills root does not exist

Text members are canonicalised to LF (the repository pins ``* text=auto eol=lf``) so the same
checkout hashes identically on any platform; binary members are hashed raw. No git history is
written, no commit is created, nothing is published.

CLI
---
``--repo-root DIR``            repository root (default: the directory of this file)
``--skills-root DIR``          override the skills root (default: <repo>/skills)
``--out FILE``                 write the ledger JSON to FILE (default: stdout only)
``--no-git``                   skip the git clean/commit/tree gates (fixtures; requires the
                               ``--ledger-commit`` and ``--ledger-tree`` overrides)
``--ledger-commit HEX40``      freeze this commit instead of the git HEAD (fixtures/audits)
``--ledger-tree HEX40``        freeze this tree instead of the git HEAD^{tree}
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LEDGER_VERSION = "PIPD-PUBLIC-PLUGIN-SOURCE-LEDGER/1"
EXPECTED_SKILLS = (
    "pipd-assurance-tqaep",
    "pipd-authority-source",
    "pipd-execution-contract",
    "pipd-package-project",
    "pipd-pd-bind",
    "pipd-pi-compile",
    "pipd-profile-tailor",
    "pipd-route-intake",
)
HEX40 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")


class FreezeRefusal(Exception):
    """A fail-closed refusal. ``code`` is the machine-checkable typed reason."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"REFUSED {code}: {detail}")
        self.code = code
        self.detail = detail


def _sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def canonical_bytes(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    """Canonical member bytes: LF-normalised for text, raw for binary."""
    if b"\x00" in data:
        return data
    try:
        data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return data
    return data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n").replace(b"\r", b"\n")


def _git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    git = shutil.which("git")
    if git is None:
        raise FreezeRefusal("GIT_UNAVAILABLE", "no `git` executable on PATH")
    proc = subprocess.run([git, "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise FreezeRefusal(
            "GIT_FAILED",
            f"`git {' '.join(args)}` exited {proc.returncode}: "
            f"{(proc.stderr or proc.stdout).strip()}",
        )
    return proc.stdout


def _walk_skill_files(repo_root: Path, skill_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Every regular file under one skill, as ``repo-relative POSIX path -> canonical sha256``."""
    files: dict[str, str] = {}
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(skill_dir, topdown=True, followlinks=False):
        dirnames.sort()
        filenames.sort()
        for d in list(dirnames):
            p = Path(dirpath) / d
            if p.is_symlink():
                raise FreezeRefusal("SYMLINK_MEMBER", str(p))
            if d.startswith(".") or d in ("__pycache__",):
                raise FreezeRefusal("HIDDEN_OR_SPECIAL_MEMBER", str(p))
        for f in filenames:
            p = Path(dirpath) / f
            st = os.lstat(p)
            if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode):
                raise FreezeRefusal("SYMLINK_MEMBER", str(p))
            if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
                raise FreezeRefusal(
                    "NON_REGULAR_FILE",
                    f"{p} is not a regular file (mode {oct(stat.S_IMODE(st.st_mode))})")
            if f.startswith(".") or f in ("__pycache__",):
                raise FreezeRefusal("HIDDEN_OR_SPECIAL_MEMBER", str(p))
            rel = p.relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
            files[rel] = _sha256_bytes(canonical_bytes(p.read_bytes()))
    return files


def _skill_entries(skills_root: Path) -> dict[str, Path]:
    if not skills_root.is_dir():
        raise FreezeRefusal("SKILLS_ROOT_MISSING", str(skills_root))
    entries: dict[str, Path] = {}
    for child in sorted(skills_root.iterdir()):
        if child.name.startswith(".") or child.name == "__pycache__":
            continue
        if child.is_symlink():
            raise FreezeRefusal("SYMLINK_MEMBER", str(child))
        if not child.is_dir():
            raise FreezeRefusal("NON_REGULAR_FILE",
                                f"{child} sits directly in the skills root and is not a skill dir")
        entries[child.name] = child
    return entries


def freeze(repo_root: Path, skills_root: Path | None = None, *, require_git: bool = True,
           commit_override: str | None = None, tree_override: str | None = None,
           repo_url_override: str | None = None,
           expected_skills: tuple[str, ...] = EXPECTED_SKILLS) -> dict:
    """Produce the frozen source ledger. Raises :class:`FreezeRefusal` on any deviation."""
    repo_root = Path(repo_root).resolve()
    skills_root = Path(skills_root).resolve() if skills_root is not None else repo_root / "skills"

    if require_git:
        top = _git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel").strip()
        if Path(top).resolve() != repo_root:
            raise FreezeRefusal("NOT_REPO_ROOT",
                                f"git top-level {top!r} != given repo root {repo_root}")
        dirty = _git(repo_root, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=normal").strip()
        if dirty:
            raise FreezeRefusal("DIRTY_WORKTREE",
                                "worktree is not clean:\n" + "\n".join(dirty.splitlines()[:20]))
        commit = _git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
        tree = _git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}").strip()
        repo_url = _git(repo_root, "remote", "get-url", "origin").strip() or "NO_REMOTE"
    else:
        if commit_override is None or tree_override is None:
            raise FreezeRefusal("FIXTURE_OVERRIDE_MISSING",
                                "--no-git requires --ledger-commit and --ledger-tree")
        commit, tree = commit_override, tree_override
        repo_url = repo_url_override or "FIXTURE_NO_GIT"

    for label, value in (("commit", commit), ("tree", tree)):
        if not HEX40.match(value):
            raise FreezeRefusal("IDENTITY_INVALID",
                                f"{label} is not 40 hex chars: {value!r}")

    entries = _skill_entries(skills_root)
    missing = [n for n in expected_skills if n not in entries]
    extra = [n for n in sorted(entries) if n not in set(expected_skills)]
    if missing or extra:
        raise FreezeRefusal("WRONG_SKILL_SET",
                            f"expected exactly {sorted(expected_skills)}; "
                            f"missing={missing} extra={extra}")

    files: dict[str, str] = {}
    for name in sorted(entries):
        files.update(_walk_skill_files(repo_root, entries[name]))

    total = sum(len(canonical_bytes((repo_root / rel).read_bytes())) for rel in files)
    return {
        "ledger_version": LEDGER_VERSION,
        "repo": repo_url,
        "commit": commit,
        "tree": tree,
        "skills": sorted(entries),
        "canonicalization": "text=LF;binary=raw",
        "file_count": len(files),
        "total_canonical_bytes": total,
        "files": files,
    }


def canonical_json(doc: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--repo-root", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
    ap.add_argument("--skills-root", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--no-git", action="store_true", help="fixture mode (no git gates)")
    ap.add_argument("--ledger-commit", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--ledger-tree", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--repo-url", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        ledger = freeze(
            Path(args.repo_root),
            Path(args.skills_root) if args.skills_root else None,
            require_git=not args.no_git,
            commit_override=args.ledger_commit,
            tree_override=args.ledger_tree,
            repo_url_override=args.repo_url,
        )
    except FreezeRefusal as exc:
        print(str(exc))
        return 2
    text = canonical_json(ledger)
    if args.out:
        out = Path(args.out)
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    sys.stdout.write(text)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Bounded writer brief — Stage B: public Skills-only plugin projection (S4POST round)

You are a **bounded writer**. Change ONLY files under "Allowed write set". Everything else —
`skills/**`, `src/**`, `schemas/**`, `dist/**`, `.hgk/**`, any existing release asset — is
forbidden. If the work seems to need a change outside the set, stop and report instead.

## Goal

Turn the existing eight skills into a **portable, deterministic, fail-closed plugin package
candidate**, plus a single-file web fallback and installation routes. Nothing here publishes
anything: the deliverable is a *candidate* whose owner-gated inputs are missing on purpose and must
make the build REFUSE rather than warn.

## Ground truth you must respect (already measured, do not re-litigate)

- `skills/pipd-*`: 8 skills, exactly 6 files each, 48 files total, no deviations.
- **Every** `SKILL.md` frontmatter carries the non-portable keys `version`, `owner`, `triggers`,
  `schemas`, `references`, `tests`. None of the eight is a subset of the portable set
  {name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools}. Therefore a byte-copy
  projection is **impossible**: each skill needs an owner-approved derivation record.
- **No image asset exists anywhere in the repo.** Do not add a binary PNG. Generate the icon
  deterministically from a tiny stdlib PNG writer (zlib + struct, no Pillow, no new dependency) and
  validate it by decoding the signature, IHDR, chunk CRCs and inflating IDAT.
- `dist/` holds 41 tracked release assets and must not be written.
- No `packaging/`, no `docs/install/`, no `plugin.json` exists yet.

## Allowed write set

## Required behaviour

1. **`freeze_public_plugin_source.py`** — emit a frozen source ledger from a clean checkout: repo,
   commit (40 hex), tree (40 hex), the exact eight skill names, and `path -> sha256` for every file

2. **`build_public_plugin.py`** — build the plugin ZIP deterministically:
   - refuse when any owner input is missing: a per-skill derivation record whose `source_sha256`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""S4POST Stage B: build the deterministic, fail-closed public Skills-only plugin candidate.

This tool turns the eight ``skills/pipd-*`` packs into ONE portable plugin ZIP. It is
fail-closed by construction: every owner-gated input that has not been supplied yet makes the build
REFUSE with a typed reason (non-zero exit), never warn. Nothing here publishes anything; the output
is a *candidate* whose receipt says ``claim_ceiling: LOCAL_PACKAGER_PASS_ONLY`` and
``official_portal_verification: NOT_EXECUTED``.

Owner-gated inputs (all missing on purpose in the checked-in candidate):
  * a per-skill derivation record in ``derivations.json`` whose ``source_sha256`` matches the
    frozen ledger (each ``SKILL.md`` carries non-portable frontmatter, so a byte-copy projection is
    impossible and every skill needs an owner-approved derivation),
  * the pinned official-schema digest (``official_schema_sha256`` must equal the sha256 of the local
    ``plugin.schema.json`` subset),
  * the publisher identity,
  * the icon digests.

Determinism: fixed ZIP metadata (1980-01-01, mode 0644, DEFLATED level 9). The archive is written
to a scratch file, read back and compared member-by-member before it is promoted into place, so two
builds from the same inputs are byte-identical.

CLI
---
``--source-root DIR``     frozen checkout (default: the repository of this file)
``--ledger FILE``         frozen source ledger from ``freeze_public_plugin_source.py``
``--source-commit HEX40`` the pinned source commit (must equal the ledger commit)
``--packaging-root DIR``  authoring directory (default: <repo>/packaging/public-plugin)
``--out-dir DIR``         release directory for the candidate ZIP (must not overlap the repo)
``--generate-icons``      (re)write the deterministic PNG icons into the packaging assets first
"""

class Refusal(Exception):
    """A fail-closed build refusal. ``code`` is the machine-checkable typed reason."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"REFUSED {code}: {detail}")
        self.code = code
        self.detail = detail


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def canonical_json_bytes(doc) -> bytes:
    return (json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode("utf-8")


def is_placeholder(value) -> bool:
    return value is None or (isinstance(value, str) and value.strip().upper() in PLACEHOLDERS)


def _path_is_symlink(path) -> bool:
    """Seam for tests: a single predicate the symlink gates consult."""
    return os.path.islink(path)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- PNG (stdlib only)
def _png_chunk(chunk_type: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    crc = zlib.crc32(chunk_type + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + chunk_type + data + struct.pack(">I", crc)


def png_icon_bytes(size: int = 128) -> bytes:
    """A deterministic RGBA icon: no Pillow, no new dependency, no wall-clock input."""
    if size < 8:
        raise ValueError("icon size must be at least 8 px")
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(size):
        raw.append(0)  # filter type 0 (None)
        for x in range(size):
            r = (x * 255) // (size - 1)
            g = (y * 255) // (size - 1)
            border = x < size // 16 or x >= size - size // 16 or y < size // 16 or y >= size - size // 16
            b = 0x10 if border else 0x60

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    default_repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    ap.add_argument("--source-root", default=str(default_repo))
    ap.add_argument("--ledger", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-commit", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--packaging-root", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--generate-icons", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    source_root = Path(args.source_root).resolve()
    packaging_root = (Path(args.packaging_root) if args.packaging_root
                      else source_root / "packaging" / "public-plugin")
    try:
        ledger = json.loads(Path(args.ledger).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"REFUSED LEDGER_UNREADABLE: {exc}")
        return 2
    try:
        report = build_plugin(
            source_root=source_root,
            ledger=ledger,
            source_commit=args.source_commit,
            packaging_root=packaging_root,
            out_dir=Path(args.out_dir),
            generate_icons=args.generate_icons,
        )
    except Refusal as exc:
        print(str(exc))
        return 2
    print(f"BUILT {report['out_zip']} sha256={report['zip_sha256']} "
          f"members={report['member_count']} "
          f"claim_ceiling={report['claim_ceiling']} "
          f"official_portal_verification={report['official_portal_verification']}")
    return 0

"C:\\Users\\user\\.cache\\codex-runtimes\\codex-primary-runtime\\dependencies\\native\\powershell\\pwsh.exe" -Command 'cd C:/Projects/Agent_Workspace/PIPD/worktrees/s4post-b-wt; Get-Content tests/test_s4ext_release_provenance.py' in C:\Projects\Agent_Workspace\PIPD\worktrees\s4post-b-wt
 succeeded in 426ms:
"""S4EXT-R1 (TT-S4EXT-001 / TT-S4EXT-003): release-provenance truth for the mount packs.

F001 of the external challenge (``PIPD-LS-SP-S4-EXTERNAL-CHALLENGE-2026-10-12-R1``) was a
CONFIRMED_DEFECT: every document of the ``v0.1.1-preview.3`` Web Mount pack declared
``tag commit 8faa64e581e8c25f5ec355475e29561847da3ead`` -- which is the ``v0.1.0-preview.2`` tag
target -- instead of the real dereference ``cbf69756d7fc90fc1cdfb3a45a1cc42cc603cb0a``. F003 was
the matching evidence gap: the only release-identity regression test pinned ``preview.2``, so no
test could observe the preview.3 mismatch.

This module closes both by making the expectation DERIVED rather than hand-written:

* the identity comes from ``docs/RELEASE_TUPLE.json``;
* the tuple's ``release_tag_target`` / ``tree`` are re-derived from the repository's own git
  objects with ``git rev-parse`` (no network, no floating branch);
* the pack documents must agree with the tuple, and the check is exercised in the NEGATIVE
  direction too (a stale value injected into a document must be refused), so a passing suite
  cannot be an artefact of a checker that always returns clean;
* ``build_source_commit`` and ``release_tag_target`` stay SEPARATE fields -- collapsing them into
  one string is the defect this module exists to prevent.

The tests never write inside the repository: a pack copy is built in a temporary directory.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT / "src") not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from tools import build_mount_pack as BMP  # noqa: E402

TUPLE_PATH = ROOT / "docs" / "RELEASE_TUPLE.json"
HEX40 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{40}")

# The line shapes that ASSERT a pack's release identity. A 40-hex token on one of these lines is a
# provenance claim and must equal the frozen tuple's release_tag_target.
IDENTITY_MARKERS = (
    "release identity:",
    "bound to `v",
    "release_tag_commit:",
    "release_tag_target:",
    "build_source_commit:",
    "| release tag target |",
    "| build source commit |",
    "| tag commit |",
    "| release tree |",
    "bind it to release",
    "(release tag target",
    "(build source commit",
    "(tag commit",
)
# Lines that DISCLOSE the historical wrong value on purpose (the erratum). They may name any sha.
DISCLOSURE_MARKERS = ("erratum", "lineage note", "previously published", "stale")


def load_tuple() -> dict:
    return json.loads(TUPLE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    """Run git against this checkout; native tool, so the path is passed Windows-style."""
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT).replace("\\", "/"), *args],
                         check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.stdout.strip()


def _sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def identity_claims(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, list[str], str]]:
    """Every (lineno, hex tokens, line) that claims identity, excluding disclosure lines."""
    claims = []
    for lineno, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        low = line.lower()
        if not any(m in low for m in IDENTITY_MARKERS):
            continue
        if any(m in low for m in DISCLOSURE_MARKERS):
            continue
        tokens = HEX40.findall(line)
        if tokens:
            claims.append((lineno, tokens, line.strip()))
    return claims


def pack_identity_problems(pack_dir: Path, entry: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Return the provenance problems for one pack directory (empty list == clean)."""
    problems: list[str] = []
    target = entry["release_tag_target"]
    build = entry["build_source_commit"]
    docs = sorted(p for p in pack_dir.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.name != "MANIFEST.sha256")
    if not docs:
        return [f"{pack_dir.name}: pack has no documents"]
    # every OTHER release's tag target is a foreign object for this pack
    foreign = {r["release_tag_target"] for r in load_tuple()["releases"]
               if r["release_id"] != entry["release_id"]}
    for doc in docs:
        text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        rel = f"{pack_dir.name}/{doc.relative_to(pack_dir).as_posix()}"
        if target not in text:
            problems.append(f"{rel}: does not carry release_tag_target {target[:12]}")
        if build not in text:
            problems.append(f"{rel}: does not carry build_source_commit {build[:12]}")
        for lineno, tokens, line in identity_claims(text):
            for token in tokens:
                if token != target and token in foreign:
                    problems.append(
                        f"{rel}:{lineno}: asserts foreign release object {token[:12]} as this "
                        f"release's identity ({line[:70]})")
    return problems


class TupleIsDerivedFromGitTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The frozen tuple must match the repository's own git objects, re-derived here."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.releases = load_tuple()["releases"]

    def test_every_tag_dereferences_to_the_recorded_target(self) -> None:
        for entry in self.releases:
            tag = entry["release_id"]
            self.assertEqual(git("rev-parse", f"{tag}^{{commit}}"), entry["release_tag_target"], tag)

    def test_every_recorded_tree_is_the_targets_tree(self) -> None:
        for entry in self.releases:
            tag = entry["release_id"]
            self.assertEqual(git("rev-parse", f"{tag}^{{tree}}"), entry["tree"], tag)

    def test_annotated_tag_object_recorded_verbatim(self) -> None:
        for entry in self.releases:
            tag = entry["release_id"]
            self.assertEqual(git("rev-parse", tag), entry["tag_object"], tag)
            kind = git("cat-file", "-t", tag)
            self.assertIn(kind, ("tag", "commit"), tag)

    def test_build_source_and_tag_target_are_separate_fields(self) -> None:
        """Collapsing them into one string IS the F001 defect; both must exist per release."""
        for entry in self.releases:
            self.assertIn("build_source_commit", entry, entry["release_id"])
            self.assertIn("release_tag_target", entry, entry["release_id"])
            self.assertNotIn("tag_commit", entry,
                             "a single collapsed `tag_commit` field is exactly what F001 broke on")

    def test_preview3_stale_value_is_the_preview2_target(self) -> None:
        by_id = {r["release_id"]: r for r in self.releases}
        self.assertEqual(by_id["v0.1.1-preview.3"]["stale_identity_in_first_shipped_asset"],
                         by_id["v0.1.0-preview.2"]["release_tag_target"])


class PackDocumentsAgreeWithTupleTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """positive: every pack document names its own release's object (F001 8/8)."""

    def test_every_pack_directory_is_identity_clean(self) -> None:
        for entry in load_tuple()["releases"]:
            if not entry.get("pack_dir"):
                continue
            pack = ROOT / entry["pack_dir"]
            self.assertTrue(pack.is_dir(), entry["pack_dir"])
            self.assertEqual(pack_identity_problems(pack, entry), [], entry["release_id"])

    def test_preview3_pack_has_all_eight_documents(self) -> None:
        entry = next(r for r in load_tuple()["releases"] if r["release_id"] == "v0.1.1-preview.3")
        pack = ROOT / entry["pack_dir"]
        docs = sorted(p.relative_to(pack).as_posix() for p in pack.rglob("*")
                      if p.is_file() and p.name != "MANIFEST.sha256")
        self.assertEqual(len(docs), 8, docs)

    def test_preview3_documents_state_the_release_tag_target(self) -> None:
        """Every one of the eight documents must name the tag it is actually shipped under.

        The superseded repair path additionally required a literal ``release tag target`` caption in
        all eight files; the served asset states the identity as *release id + tag commit*, and the
        pack bytes are the published asset, so the caption is not demanded. The substantive rule is
        kept in FULL: no subset escape and no floor — every document is checked.
        """
        entry = next(r for r in load_tuple()["releases"] if r["release_id"] == "v0.1.1-preview.3")
        pack = ROOT / entry["pack_dir"]
        docs = sorted(p for p in pack.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.name != "MANIFEST.sha256")
        self.assertEqual(len(docs), 8, docs)
        for doc in docs:
            text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIn(entry["release_tag_target"], text, doc.name)

    def test_the_replacement_is_corroborated_outside_our_own_fields(self) -> None:
        """The in-place replacement must be backed by a producer record, not only our own metadata.

        ``asset_replaced_in_place`` and the digests in the tuple are written by this repository, so
        they can only corroborate themselves. The release-correction round left a producer log with
        the replaced asset's id and the new bytes; pin those, so the claim that a replacement
        happened cannot rest on our own boolean alone.
        """
        log = ROOT / ".hgk/rounds/S4R2M-20261012-merge-and-preview3/release/PUBLISH_REPLACE.log"
        self.assertTrue(log.is_file(), str(log))
        text = log.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        entry = next(r for r in load_tuple()["releases"] if r["release_id"] == "v0.1.1-preview.3")
        self.assertIn("631301834", text, "the replaced asset id is not recorded")
        self.assertIn(entry["published_asset_sha256"], text,
                      "the served digest is not recorded in the producer log")


class StaleIdentityIsRefusedTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """negative: the pre-repair preview.3 text and a re-injected stale value must be refused."""

    def _preview3(self) -> tuple[dict, Path]:
        entry = next(r for r in load_tuple()["releases"] if r["release_id"] == "v0.1.1-preview.3")
        return entry, ROOT / entry["pack_dir"]

    def test_stale_value_no_longer_asserted_anywhere(self) -> None:
        entry, pack = self._preview3()
        stale = entry["stale_identity_in_first_shipped_asset"]
        for doc in sorted(p for p in pack.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.name != "MANIFEST.sha256"):
            for lineno, _tokens, line in identity_claims(doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
                self.assertNotIn(stale, line, f"{doc.name}:{lineno} still asserts the stale object")

    def test_reinjecting_the_stale_value_is_refused(self) -> None:
        entry, pack = self._preview3()
        stale = entry["stale_identity_in_first_shipped_asset"]
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            copy = Path(td) / pack.name
            shutil.copytree(pack, copy)
            doc = copy / "README_MOUNT.md"
            text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            doc.write_text(text.replace(entry["release_tag_target"], stale), encoding="utf-8")
            problems = pack_identity_problems(copy, entry)
            self.assertTrue(problems, "a document re-naming preview.2's object must be refused")
            self.assertTrue(any("foreign release object" in p or "does not carry" in p
                                for p in problems), problems)

    def test_replacing_only_the_version_string_is_refused(self) -> None:
        """The pre-repair failure mode exactly: bump the version, keep the old commit.

        Also guards against a future edit that deletes the commit from the document entirely:
        dropping the identity is refused as well as mis-stating it.
        """
        entry, pack = self._preview3()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            copy = Path(td) / pack.name
            shutil.copytree(pack, copy)
            doc = copy / "SKILL.md"
            text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            # keep the version banner, remove every trace of the correct object
            doc.write_text(text.replace(entry["release_tag_target"], ""), encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertTrue(pack_identity_problems(copy, entry))

    def test_the_old_preview2_only_checker_would_have_passed(self) -> None:
        """Why F003 mattered: preview.2's own pack was clean, so an old-value-only pin saw nothing.

        The preview.2 pack legitimately names its own target (which IS the stale value for
        preview.3). A check that only knows preview.2 therefore cannot detect the preview.3 defect;
        the tuple-driven check above does.
        """
        p2 = next(r for r in load_tuple()["releases"] if r["release_id"] == "v0.1.0-preview.2")
        pack2 = ROOT / p2["pack_dir"]
        self.assertEqual(pack_identity_problems(pack2, p2), [])
        entry3, _ = self._preview3()
        self.assertEqual(p2["release_tag_target"], entry3["stale_identity_in_first_shipped_asset"])


class DistributionArtifactTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """What is served now is the corrected asset; what was served first is kept as history."""

    def _preview3(self) -> dict:
        return next(r for r in load_tuple()["releases"] if r["release_id"] == "v0.1.1-preview.3")

    def test_published_zips_are_byte_identical_to_the_recorded_digest(self) -> None:
        for entry in load_tuple()["releases"]:
            if not entry.get("zip"):
                continue
            zip_path = ROOT / entry["zip"]
            self.assertTrue(zip_path.is_file(), entry["zip"])
            if entry.get("published_asset_sha256"):
                self.assertEqual(_sha256_file(zip_path), entry["published_asset_sha256"],
                                 f"{entry['zip']} differs from the digest recorded for the served asset")

    def test_current_published_asset_matches_its_sidecar(self) -> None:
        entry = self._preview3()
        zip_path = ROOT / entry["zip"]
        sidecar = zip_path.with_name(zip_path.name + ".sha256")
        self.assertTrue(sidecar.is_file(), sidecar.name)
        self.assertEqual(_sha256_file(zip_path), sidecar.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split()[0])

    def test_the_replacement_is_logged_and_the_first_shipped_digest_is_preserved(self) -> None:
        entry = self._preview3()
        self.assertTrue(entry["asset_replaced_in_place"])
        record = ROOT / entry["asset_replacement_record"]
        self.assertTrue(record.is_file(), entry["asset_replacement_record"])
        first = entry["first_shipped_asset_sha256"]
        self.assertTrue(first and first != entry["published_asset_sha256"],
                        "the historical digest must be kept separate from the served one")
        self.assertIn("superseded_candidate_zip", entry)
        self.assertFalse((ROOT / entry["superseded_candidate_zip"]).is_file(),
                         "the superseded separate-rebuild candidate must not appear to be shipped")

    def test_rebuild_from_the_tree_reproduces_the_served_asset(self) -> None:
        """Two rebuilds agree byte-for-byte, and they equal the asset actually served."""
        entry = self._preview3()
        pack = ROOT / entry["pack_dir"]
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            tmp = Path(td)
            digests = []
            for name in ("a", "b"):
                copy = tmp / name / pack.name
                shutil.copytree(pack, copy)
                out = tmp / f"{name}.zip"
                BMP.build_pack(copy, out)
                digests.append(_sha256_file(out))
            self.assertEqual(digests[0], digests[1], "the builder is not deterministic")
            self.assertEqual(digests[0], _sha256_file(ROOT / entry["zip"]),
                             "the served asset must be reproducible from the checked-in tree")

    def test_no_member_of_the_served_asset_captured_crlf(self) -> None:
        """The historical defect was CRLF-captured members; the served asset must carry none."""
        entry = self._preview3()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(ROOT / entry["zip"]) as zf:
            offenders = [n for n in zf.namelist() if b"\r\n" in zf.read(n)]
        self.assertEqual(offenders, [], f"CRLF members in the served asset: {offenders[:3]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

"""Deterministic validation: schema + semantic invariants over the 19 families.

Deterministic only: no LLM judge is consulted here (總藍圖 §5.9.1 responsibility split).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
import re
from typing import Any

from . import registry
from .errors import ValidationFail

CLAIM_LADDER = ["PROMPT_COMPILE_PASS", "HGK_ADMITTED", "RUNTIME_READY", "LOCAL_QUALIFIED",
                "INDEPENDENT_PASS", "PUBLICATION_APPROVED", "RELEASED", "PRODUCTION_VERIFIED"]
RELEASE_BOUND = ("PI-PKG", "PD-PKG", "ECP", "TQAEP", "ConstructionContract")

# CE-2 refinement (checker counterexample CE-CODEX-TRACE-WIDENING). Two DISTINCT concepts that
# used to be conflated into one list: "fields excluded from the body hash" and "fields that are
# not part of the record at all". They overlap only on `_profile_meta`.
#
# HASH_EXCLUDED_FIELDS -- the fields the body hash does NOT cover: the universal identity fields
#   (recomputed after sealing), the derived `trace` relation (it carries the parent hash, so it
#   cannot sit inside the hash it references) and the `_profile_meta` sidecar. This is the
#   HASH-EXCLUSION set ONLY; it says nothing about which fields a schema declares. `_body_hash`
#   and `pipeline._seal` both reference THIS object, so the hash and its recomputation stay one
#   definition and cannot diverge.
HASH_EXCLUDED_FIELDS = ("subject_id", "version", "content_hash", "schema_version", "trace",
                        "_profile_meta")

# NON_RECORD_SIDECARS -- the fields the pipeline emits for the operator/registry that NO schema
#   declares at all. Today that is exactly `_profile_meta`. `validate_record` strips ONLY this
#   set before the schema check, so a field that is hash-excluded but IS declared by the schema
#   (the identity fields, or `trace` on PI-PKG) remains schema-enforced, and an undeclared
#   `trace` on PD-PKG/ECP/TQAEP is again rejected by `additionalProperties: false`, exactly as
#   the published validator behaves.
NON_RECORD_SIDECARS = ("_profile_meta",)


def _validator(schema: dict[str, Any]):
    try:
        from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover
        raise ValidationFail(f"jsonschema unavailable: {exc}") from exc
    return Draft202012Validator(schema)


def validate_record(contract: str, record: dict[str, Any], schemas_dir: Path | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Return a list of deterministic findings; empty list == schema-valid.

    Schema validation runs on a COPY of the record with the genuine non-record sidecars
    (``NON_RECORD_SIDECARS`` - today only ``_profile_meta``) removed, so a bundle assembled from
    the compilers' own stdout (which carries ``_profile_meta``) is held to its declared field set
    instead of tripping ``additionalProperties: false``. This is exactly the "stripped before
    validation" behavior ``pipeline`` already declares.

    ``NON_RECORD_SIDECARS`` is deliberately NOT the same set as ``HASH_EXCLUDED_FIELDS``: a field
    can be excluded from the body hash (``trace``, the identity fields) yet still be part of the
    record's contract, so its presence must remain schema-enforced. Only the genuine non-record
    sidecar ``_profile_meta`` is stripped; the defensive "unless the schema declares it" guard
    keeps that safe even if a future schema chooses to declare a sidecar. This closes CE-2 without
    widening the accepted input.
    """
    schema = registry.load_schema(contract, schemas_dir)
    v = _validator(schema)
    declared = set(schema.get("properties") or {})
    body = {k: val for k, val in record.items()
            if k not in NON_RECORD_SIDECARS or k in declared}
    findings = []
    for err in sorted(v.iter_errors(body), key=lambda e: list(e.absolute_path)):

def _escapes(rel: str) -> bool:
    parts = rel.replace("\\", "/").split("/")
    return (rel.startswith("/") or "\\" in rel or ":" in rel or ".." in parts
            or any(part == "" for part in parts) or parts[0] in (".", ""))

"""WO-S4R2M-DOC-CAL-01: the front page routes a reader down one of two paths, and describes
``--root`` the way the parser actually behaves.

The README's ``## Choose your path: CLI or Skills`` section must separate the *published wheel*
(the CLI + 19 installed schemas, and nothing loaded into a web host) from the *candidate-branch
mount pack* (document consumption, not a published release asset, native load not demonstrated).
The README's ``--root`` wording must no longer claim the option *always* precedes the subcommand:
``src/pipd_ls_sp/cli.py`` adds a subcommand-local ``--root`` (``dest="sub_root"``) to ``project``
and ``export``, and the dispatcher resolves ``getattr(args, "sub_root", None) or args.root``.

These tests are the machine-checkable half of both claims. They read README text only and drive the
CLI surface (``python -m pipd_ls_sp.cli``) through ``sys.executable`` with this repository's ``src``
on ``PYTHONPATH``, so they never depend on a machine-specific interpreter path. They touch no
``src/**``, ``schemas/**`` or network.

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SRC = ROOT / "src"
if str(SRC) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(SRC))
README = ROOT / "README.md"

ENV = {**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(SRC),
       "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1", "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8"}


def _readme_text() -> str:
    return README.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def _headings(text: str) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Line index of each ``## `` heading, keyed by its exact title text."""
    found: dict[str, int] = {}
    for i, line in enumerate(text.splitlines()):
        if line.startswith("## "):
            found[line[3:].strip()] = i
    return found


def _section(text: str, title: str) -> str:
    """The body of the ``## <title>`` section, up to the next ``## `` heading."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    start = None
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() == f"## {title}":
            start = i + 1
            break
    if start is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"section {title!r} not found")
    end = len(lines)
    for j in range(start, len(lines)):
        if lines[j].startswith("## "):
            end = j
            break
    return "\n".join(lines[start:end])


def _cli(cwd: Path, *args: str) -> "subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]":
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", "-m", "pipd_ls_sp.cli", *args],
                          cwd=str(cwd), env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8")


class ChooseYourPathSection(unittest.TestCase):
    """The routing heading exists, and sits between ``## Start here`` and ``## Quickstart``."""

    def test_new_heading_exists_between_start_here_and_quickstart(self) -> None:
        headings = _headings(_readme_text())
        self.assertIn("Start here", headings)
        self.assertIn("Choose your path: CLI or Skills", headings)
        self.assertIn("Quickstart", headings)
        self.assertLess(
            headings["Start here"],
            headings["Choose your path: CLI or Skills"],
            "the routing section must follow `## Start here`",
        )
        self.assertLess(
            headings["Choose your path: CLI or Skills"],
            headings["Quickstart"],
            "the routing section must precede `## Quickstart`",
        )

    def test_section_names_both_paths_and_their_artefacts(self) -> None:
        section = _section(_readme_text(), "Choose your path: CLI or Skills")
        # CLI / headless harness: the immutable published wheel + its digest.
        self.assertIn("v0.1.1-preview.3", section)
        self.assertIn("pipd_ls_sp-0.1.1a3-py3-none-any.whl", section)
        self.assertIn(
            "e8ca509d9014e57536d18bc103d91d06e4cd40e4f2e3ef0cec6a7a083fafe7ec", section)
        self.assertIn("doctor", section)
        # Skills / document consumption: the candidate-branch mount pack, not a release asset.
        self.assertIn("dist/mount/PIPD-LS-SP_S4_WEB_MOUNT_v0.1.1-preview.3.zip", section)
        self.assertIn("MANIFEST.sha256", section)

    def test_cli_path_is_not_claimed_to_load_skills_into_a_host(self) -> None:
        section = _section(_readme_text(), "Choose your path: CLI or Skills")
        self.assertRegex(
            section,

            "the section must say the wheel does not load the skills into a web host",
        )
        self.assertIn("19", section)

    def test_skills_path_names_manual_route_and_does_not_assert_native_load(self) -> None:

        # The manual / Knowledge document route must be named.

        self.assertIn("SKILL.md", section)
        self.assertIn("PIPD_LS_SP_QUICKSTART_PROMPT.md", section)
        # From preview.3 the pack is genuinely a release asset of the tag, so the old "not a
        # published release asset" wording is factually superseded. The protective intent stays:
        # the pack must be named as an asset of the same tag, and native load is still unclaimed.

                r"\b(is|was|has been)\b[^.\n]*\b(demonstrated|verified|confirmed|supported|proven)\b",
                section,
                re.I,
            ),
            "the section must not claim a native skill load was demonstrated",
        )
        # The document path does not run the CLI on the reader's machine.
        self.assertRegex(section, r"does \*\*not\*\* execute `pipd`")


class RootWordingIsTruthful(unittest.TestCase):
    """The README no longer states the absolute ``--root``-must-always-precede rule."""

    def test_no_absolute_global_must_precede_claim(self) -> None:
        text = _readme_text()
        # The old absolute phrasing: an emphasised GLOBAL paired with an unconditional rule.
        self.assertNotRegex(text, r"--root` is a \*\*GLOBAL\*\* option",
                            "the blanket `--root` is GLOBAL claim is still present")
        for line in text.splitlines():
            if re.search(r"--root", line, re.I) and re.search(r"must precede", line, re.I):
                self.assertNotRegex(
                    line, r"GLOBAL",
                    f"--root must-precede is still phrased as a blanket GLOBAL rule: {line!r}",
                )

    def test_corrected_statement_names_project_and_export_exception(self) -> None:
        text = _readme_text()
        # The corrected sentence spans several wrapped lines; take it as a region.
        m = re.search(
            r"For `init`.*?accept `--root` after the\s+subcommand",
            text,
            re.S,
        )
        self.assertIsNotNone(m, "the corrected --root sentence is missing")
        sentence = m.group(0)
        self.assertIn("additionally", sentence)
        self.assertRegex(
            sentence, r"`project` and `export`\s+\*\*additionally\*\* accept `--root`")
        for cmd in ("init", "intake", "profile", "compile-pi", "bind-pd",
                    "compile-ecp", "compile-tqaep", "validate", "doctor"):
            self.assertIn(
                f"`{cmd}`", sentence,
                f"the corrected statement must name `{cmd}` in the global-option list",
            )
        self.assertIn("`--root` is a global option", sentence)


class DocumentedRootFormsRun(unittest.TestCase):
    """The three documented positives exit 0; a refused form exits non-zero."""

    def test_three_positives_exit_zero_and_refusal_exits_nonzero(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="pipd_s4r2m_route_") as tmp:
            cwd = Path(tmp)  # scratch dir OUTSIDE the repository; `./demo` is relative to it
            init = _cli(cwd, "--root", "./demo", "init")
            self.assertEqual(init.returncode, 0,
                             f"`pipd --root ./demo init` failed: {init.stdout[:300]}")
            for label, args in (
                ("project", ("project", "--root", "./demo", "--dry-run")),
                ("export", ("export", "--root", "./demo", "--dry-run")),
            ):
                proc = _cli(cwd, *args)
                self.assertEqual(
                    proc.returncode, 0,
                    f"`pipd {label} --root ./demo --dry-run` failed: {proc.stdout[:300]}",
                )
            refused = _cli(cwd, "init", "--root", "./demo")
            self.assertNotEqual(
                refused.returncode, 0,
                "`pipd init --root ./demo` must be refused (init has no subcommand-local --root)",
            )

"""POST-F01 quickstart regression: the checksum step must cover exactly what was downloaded.

The published ``v0.1.0-preview.2`` ``SHA256SUMS`` lists three assets (the wheel, the source
zip, the preview notes) while the README quickstart fetches only the wheel and ``SHA256SUMS``.
A bare ``sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`` therefore exits non-zero with two "FAILED open or read"
lines. These tests pin the repaired contract and never touch the network:

  * every file a checksum command reads as input is a file the same block downloads;
  * the published wheel digest literal appears in both the bash and the PowerShell blocks;
  * ``pipd --root`` still precedes the subcommand everywhere it appears.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT / "src") not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
README = ROOT / "README.md"

PUBLISHED_WHEEL_DIGEST = "e8ca509d9014e57536d18bc103d91d06e4cd40e4f2e3ef0cec6a7a083fafe7ec"
WHEEL = "pipd_ls_sp-0.1.1a3-py3-none-any.whl"
SHA256SUMS = "SHA256SUMS"

def _readme_text() -> str:
    return README.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def _fenced_blocks(text: str, lang: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return the bodies of every ```lang fenced code block, in order."""
    pattern = re.compile(r"^```" + re.escape(lang) + r"[ \t]*\n(.*?)^```[ \t]*$", re.M | re.S)
    return pattern.findall(text)


def _download_set(block: str) -> set[str]:
    """Files a shell block downloads: curl (any flags, incl. ``-fsSLO``) / Invoke-WebRequest /
    ``--output``. The filename is the trailing path segment of the destination."""
    names: set[str] = set()
    for line in block.splitlines():
        if line.strip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        if re.search(r"\bcurl\b", line):
            for match in re.finditer(r"\"([^\"]+)\"", line):
                names.add(Path(match.group(1)).name)
        for match in re.finditer(r"-OutFile\s+\"?([^\s\"']+)\"?", line):
            names.add(Path(match.group(1)).name)
        for match in re.finditer(r"--output[= ]\s*\"?([^\s\"']+)\"?", line):
            names.add(Path(match.group(1)).name)
    return {Path(n).name for n in names}


def _checksum_input_set(block: str) -> set[str]:
    """Files a checksum command reads as input in this block."""
    reads: set[str] = set()
    for line in block.splitlines():
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith("#"):
            continue
        # POSIX: `... | sha256sum -c` verifies the lines piped in; the piped source file is
        # the checksum command's ONLY input, the digest-listed assets are NOT opened.
        if re.search(r"sha256sum\s+-c\s+-", line):
            for match in re.finditer(r"(\S+)\s*\|\s*sha256sum\s+-c\s+-", line):
                reads.add(Path(match.group(1)).name)
            continue
        # POSIX: `sha256sum -c <file>` opens <file>; if it is a sums file, every asset it
        # lists must itself have been downloaded.
        for match in re.finditer(r"sha256sum\s+-c\s+(\S+)", line):
            target = Path(match.group(1)).name
            if target == SHA256SUMS:
                reads |= _sums_entries(block)
            else:
                reads.add(target)
        # PowerShell: Get-FileHash -Path <file> opens <file>.
        for match in re.finditer(r"Get-FileHash\b[^\n]*?-Path\s+\"?([^\s\"']+)\"?", line):
            reads.add(Path(match.group(1)).name)
    return reads


def _sums_entries(block: str) -> set[str]:
    """Asset names referenced by the embedded published SHA256SUMS listing, if any."""
    names: set[str] = set()
    for match in re.finditer(r"^\s*[0-9a-f]{64}\s+\*?(\S+)\s*$", block, re.M):
        names.add(Path(match.group(1)).name)
    return names


class QuickstartChecksumScope(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_block_download_and_checksum_sets(self) -> None:
        text = _readme_text()
        bash_blocks = _fenced_blocks(text, "bash")
        ps_blocks = _fenced_blocks(text, "powershell")

        self.assertTrue(bash_blocks, "README has no ```bash quickstart block")
        self.assertTrue(ps_blocks, "README has no ```powershell quickstart block")

        quickstart_bash = next((b for b in bash_blocks if WHEEL in b and SHA256SUMS in b), None)
        self.assertIsNotNone(quickstart_bash, "no bash block fetches the wheel + SHA256SUMS")
        quickstart_ps = next((b for b in ps_blocks if WHEEL in b and SHA256SUMS in b), None)
        self.assertIsNotNone(quickstart_ps, "no powershell block fetches the wheel + SHA256SUMS")

        for label, block in (("bash", quickstart_bash), ("powershell", quickstart_ps)):
            with self.subTest(block=label):
                downloads = _download_set(block)
                checks = _checksum_input_set(block)
                # (a) the checksum command must cover exactly what was downloaded
                self.assertTrue(checks, f"{label}: no checksum command parsed")
                self.assertLessEqual(
                    checks,
                    downloads,
                    f"{label}: checksum reads {sorted(checks - downloads)} but the block only "
                    f"downloads {sorted(downloads)}",
                )
                self.assertIn(SHA256SUMS, downloads, f"{label}: SHA256SUMS is not downloaded")
                self.assertIn(WHEEL, downloads, f"{label}: the wheel is not downloaded")

    def test_published_digest_literal_in_both_blocks(self) -> None:
        text = _readme_text()
        bash_blocks = _fenced_blocks(text, "bash")
        ps_blocks = _fenced_blocks(text, "powershell")
        self.assertIn(PUBLISHED_WHEEL_DIGEST, text)
        self.assertTrue(
            any(PUBLISHED_WHEEL_DIGEST in b for b in bash_blocks),
            "published digest literal missing from the bash block",
        )
        self.assertTrue(
            any(PUBLISHED_WHEEL_DIGEST in b for b in ps_blocks),
            "published digest literal missing from the PowerShell block",
        )

    def test_unverified_one_line_install_is_present_and_labels_itself(self) -> None:
        text = _readme_text()
        url = (
            "https://github.com/shw097-team/PIPD-LS-SP/releases/download/"
            "v0.1.1-preview.3/pipd_ls_sp-0.1.1a3-py3-none-any.whl"
        )
        self.assertIn(f'python -m pip install "{url}"', text)
        lowered = text.lower()
        self.assertIn("no hash verification", lowered)

    def test_root_precedes_subcommand(self) -> None:
        text = _readme_text()
        for line in text.splitlines():
            stripped = line.strip()
            if "pipd --root" in stripped:
                # `--root` must be immediately followed by its value, then a subcommand.
                self.assertRegex(
                    stripped,
                    r"pipd --root \S+ \S+",
                    f"--root is not before the subcommand: {stripped!r}",
                )


class QuickstartBashFailFast(unittest.TestCase):
    """R1 (F07): the bash quickstart must fail fast and activate portably.

    On Windows ``.venv/bin/activate`` does not exist, so a bare ``. .venv/bin/activate`` exits
    non-zero while the unfailed block continues and ``pip install`` lands in the GLOBAL
    interpreter. The block must therefore (1) start with ``set -e`` so the first failing step
    aborts it, and (2) activate with a POSIX-or-Windows fallback so it never sources a
    path that does not exist on the host.
    """

    def _quickstart_bash(self) -> str:
        text = _readme_text()
        block = next(
            (b for b in _fenced_blocks(text, "bash") if WHEEL in b and SHA256SUMS in b), None)
        self.assertIsNotNone(block, "no bash block fetches the wheel + SHA256SUMS")
        return block

    def test_block_starts_with_set_e(self) -> None:
        lines = self._quickstart_bash().splitlines()
        self.assertTrue(lines, "bash quickstart block is empty")
        self.assertTrue(
            lines[0].startswith("set -e"),
            f"bash quickstart block must start with `set -e` (fail fast); first line is "
            f"{lines[0]!r}",
        )

    def test_block_activates_portably_with_windows_fallback(self) -> None:
        lines = self._quickstart_bash().splitlines()
        self.assertTrue(
            any("||" in ln and ".venv/Scripts/activate" in ln for ln in lines),
            "bash quickstart block has no line that falls back to `.venv/Scripts/activate` "
            "(the Windows layout)",
        )

    def test_no_bare_posix_only_activate(self) -> None:
        # A bare `. .venv/bin/activate` (no fallback) exits non-zero on Windows and — absent a
        # failing-fast guard — lets the block continue into a GLOBAL install.
        for line in self._quickstart_bash().splitlines():
            code = line.split("#", 1)[0]
            if ".venv/bin/activate" in code:
                self.assertIn(
                    "||",
                    code,
                    f"a POSIX-only `.venv/bin/activate` line can fail silently: {line!r}",
                )


class QuickstartPowerShellFailFast(unittest.TestCase):
    """R2 (F07, PowerShell): the PowerShell quickstart must fail fast.

    Under PowerShell ``$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`` alone is NOT enough: native commands
    (``python -m venv``, ``python -m pip install``, ``pipd ...``) can exit non-zero without
    raising, so the block must ALSO guard each native step on ``$LASTEXITCODE``. These tests pin
    both halves of that contract. No network, no host interpreter — README text only.
    """

    def _quickstart_ps(self) -> str:
        text = _readme_text()
        block = next(
            (b for b in _fenced_blocks(text, "powershell") if WHEEL in b and SHA256SUMS in b), None)
        self.assertIsNotNone(block, "no powershell block fetches the wheel + SHA256SUMS")
        return block

    def _code_lines(self, block: str) -> list[str]:
        """Lines with comments stripped and blanks removed."""
        out: list[str] = []
        for line in block.splitlines():
            code = line.split("#", 1)[0].strip()
            if code:
                out.append(code)
        return out

    def test_first_code_line_sets_error_action_preference_stop(self) -> None:
        lines = self._code_lines(self._quickstart_ps())
        self.assertTrue(lines, "powershell quickstart block is empty")
        first = lines[0]
        self.assertIn(
            "$ErrorActionPreference",
            first,
            f"powershell block must set $ErrorActionPreference first (fail fast); first code "
            f"line is {first!r}",
        )
        self.assertRegex(
            first,
            r"\$ErrorActionPreference\s*=\s*['\"]Stop['\"]",
            f"powershell block must set $ErrorActionPreference to 'Stop'; first code line is "
            f"{first!r}",
        )

    def test_every_native_command_is_last_exit_code_guarded(self) -> None:
        # $ErrorActionPreference does not trap native-command failures in this host's pwsh
        # ($PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference is False), so every native step must be
        # followed by an explicit `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw ... }` guard. A native step
        # is any visible python/pipd invocation.
        lines = self._code_lines(self._quickstart_ps())
        native = [
            i for i, ln in enumerate(lines)
            if re.match(r"(python\b|pipd\b)", ln) and "LASTEXITCODE" not in ln
        ]
        self.assertTrue(native, "no native steps parsed from the powershell quickstart block")
        for i in native:
            nxt = lines[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(lines) else ""
            self.assertRegex(
                nxt,
                r"\$LASTEXITCODE\s+-ne\s+0",
                f"native step is not guarded on $LASTEXITCODE: {lines[i]!r} (next line {nxt!r})",
            )
            self.assertIn("throw", nxt, f"guard does not throw: {nxt!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class ReadmeIsPortableTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The README's copy-paste block must not depend on the author's machine."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.readme = (ROOT / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def test_readme_has_no_absolute_developer_paths(self) -> None:
        offenders = [ln for ln in self.readme.splitlines()
                     if re.search(r"C:[\\/]Users[\\/]user|Agent_Workspace|PIPD-postrelease-wt",
                                  ln)]
        self.assertEqual(offenders, [], f"README still pins developer paths: {offenders[:3]}")

    def test_readme_points_at_the_portable_scripts(self) -> None:
        for name in ("examples/first-run/run.sh", "examples/first-run/run.ps1"):
            self.assertIn(name, self.readme, f"README must reference {name}")

# Bounded writer — Stage B lane B4 (resumed round): official Agent Plugins manifest conformance

You are a **bounded writer** working in `C:/Projects/Agent_Workspace/PIPD/worktrees/s4post-b-wt`
(branch `feat/s4post-triple-upgrade-20261012`). Change ONLY files under "Allowed write set".

## Why this lane exists (measured, not assumed)
The round downloaded the REAL vendor schema (Agent Plugins 1.0.0) to
`.hgk/rounds/S4POST-20261012-postrepair-recheck-and-triple-upgrade/stage-b/vendor/plugin.schema.json`,
sha256 `0a4aad95ce337878ad38802ebf0daa3fde76abe3f65400c86bcbb1ec0b3ab883`, 1805 bytes.
Its constraints: `required: ["$schema","name"]`, `additionalProperties: false`, and the ONLY permitted
top-level properties are `$schema, name, version, description, author, homepage, repository, license,
keywords, extensions`. `name` must match `^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9.-]*[a-z0-9])?$` with no `--` and no `..`.

The manifest currently emitted as the package root
(`packaging/public-plugin/plugin.json`, schema id `PIPD-PUBLIC-PLUGIN-MANIFEST/1`, keys
`plugin_id/display_name/skills/official_schema_sha256/publisher/icons/release`) is PIPD's OWN internal
manifest. **As the plugin root `plugin.json` it would be REJECTED by the vendor schema.** That is the
gap this lane closes: the package must carry a real Agent Plugins 1.0 root manifest, and PIPD's own
release bookkeeping must move into the vendor-blessed `extensions` namespace.
